tools.name: minerva_pcb_set_board_layers
tools.description: Declare the board's copper layer stack. Accepts either `layers` (explicit canonical stack, e.g. ["top","in1","in2","bottom"] — top first, bottom last, inners contiguous from in1) or `count` (total copper layers; 4 builds top,in1,in2,bottom). Refuses malformed stacks, and refuses shrinking while traces/zones still occupy a removed layer (delete or re-layer that copper first). Undoable. The reply carries the declared stack. Whether a DEPTH is fabricable is the board's selected rule profile's capabilities.max_copper_layers (a profile declaring none is 2-layer; jlcpcb-4layer declares 4), enforced at compile — declaring here never bypasses that gate. Read the current stack from minerva_pcb_board_check or minerva_pcb_get_image metadata.

count.description: Total copper layer count (2..32); builds the canonical stack for that count. Provide this OR layers — supplying BOTH is refused (mutually exclusive spellings of one declaration), as is a count outside 2..32.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_pin_info
tools.description: Pin inspector parity tool: returns the SAME info the canvas hover card shows for a pin — footprint geometry pin name, net, net members, and touching traces (a trace on the pin's net whose COPPER reaches the land — its swept width against the pad outline, the same rule the connectivity DRC's dangling-endpoint credit reads, so a run driven THROUGH the pad counts and a run stopping short of it does not) — plus approach_sides (the sides, north/east/south/west in the board frame, from which a board-rule-width trace can reach the pad clear of its OWN component's other pads at the declared clearance: an LGA column pad reports only its outer side, a lone pad all four — the same rows bus_target_guidance carries per candidate) and display_name computed by the exact display rule the UI uses (geometry pin_name > net > "(unconnected)"). Identify the pin either by ref or by a board point (x_mm/y_mm, hit-tests the nearest pad). Reply also carries the pad's world position in board mm, as position:{x_mm,y_mm} — the pad row's spelling since where it used to be a bare [x,y] pair. THE REPLY IS THE PAD ROW: {kind:'pad', ref, component, pin, net, position:{x_mm,y_mm}, layer, side, approach_sides, roles} — the same shape minerva_pcb_get_selection and minerva_pcb_free_pins return — plus this tool's own extras: pin_name, net_members, trace_ids, trace_count, display_name. `side` is which side/COLUMN of its own component the pad sits on and is NOT approach_sides, which is which way a trace may leave it. `roles` is what the board's own pin table says the pin is for (strapping, uart_console, jtag, onboard_led, adc), [] when the board declares nothing.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_component
tools.description: Add a component to the PCB. TWO KINDS OF PART, and the choice decides whether the board can be fabricated. (1) BY LIBRARY REF — pass footprint:"LibNick:PartName" (e.g. "Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm:PinHeader_1x02_P2.54mm_Vertical"). The ref is resolved through the SAME seed/wip/user library chain the worker compiles against, and the part lands with the library's real pads, silk and courtyard: fabricable immediately, board_drc and the pour fill stay computable. An unresolvable ref REFUSES BY NAME and adds nothing (minerva_pcb_footprint_report shows what the library has; minerva_pcb_acquire_footprint fetches an official KiCad part it does not). On a library ref the FOOTPRINT decides the pad layout, so pin_count / pin_names / pad_type / pad_spacing / row_spacing / width / height are ignored and named back in the reply's `ignored`. (2) BY SKETCH TYPE — one of RESISTOR, CAPACITOR, IC_DIP, IC_QFP, SWITCH, CONNECTOR, LED, DIODE, TRANSISTOR, HEADER, MOUNTING_HOLE, MODULE. These build ESTIMATED geometry with NO library behind them; the hermetic worker refuses such a part by name, and that refusal makes the WHOLE board's geometric DRC and every pour fill indeterminate until the part resolves or goes. Legitimate for sketching a placement before the footprint is chosen — never for a board you intend to build. EVERY reply carries `geometry:{fabricable, source:'library'|'authored'|'sketch'|'mechanical', footprint, pad_count, note?}` — read it: a sketch part says so HERE, at add time, and the panel names it in its status line until it is fixed. SNAP DISCLOSURE: when the grid snap lands the part somewhere other than requested, the reply carries snapped:true + requested:[x,y] beside the landed coordinates — always read the reply's coordinates as the truth.

id.description: Component ID (e.g., 'R15', 'U3'). Auto-generated if not specified.

footprint.description: PREFER a library footprint ref "LibNick:PartName" (e.g. "Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm:PinHeader_1x02_P2.54mm_Vertical") — real pads and silk, fabricable immediately, refused by name if the library does not have it. The generic SKETCH types (RESISTOR, CAPACITOR, IC_DIP, IC_QFP, SWITCH, CONNECTOR, LED, DIODE, TRANSISTOR, HEADER, MOUNTING_HOLE, MODULE) build estimated geometry the worker cannot fabricate, which turns the whole board's geometric DRC and every pour fill indeterminate.

pad_type.description: Pad type for placeholder geometry (default: tht). Used when pin_count is set on non-specialised footprint types.

pad_spacing.description: Centre-to-centre pad spacing in mm (default: 2.54). Used with generic pin layout.

row_spacing.description: Row-to-row spacing for dual-row layouts in mm (default: 7.62). Used with generic pin layout.

pin_names.description: Custom pin names (e.g., ['GND', 'VCC', 'SDA', 'SCL'] for a 4-pin header)

snap_to_grid.description: Whether to snap position to grid (default: true). Set to false for exact positioning.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_move_component
tools.description: Move a component to an absolute position. Requires editor_name from minerva_list_editors and component names from minerva_pcb_get_components. FREEFORM: snap_to_grid:false lands the part exactly where asked, no grid — align a pad row with another part's off-grid row so a 2-pin span routes with ZERO bends. SNAP DISCLOSURE: when the grid snap lands the part somewhere other than requested, the reply carries snapped:true + requested:[x,y] beside the landed coordinates — always read the reply's coordinates as the truth. On success the reply may carry dangling_copper: committed trace endpoints that sat on this component's (or its group members') pads before the move and now touch none of them [{trace_id, net, at:[x,y], component_id, message}] — copper does not follow parts; delete (minerva_pcb_delete_traces) or reroute those traces before routing new work. On success the reply carries pads: [PAD ROW,...] — EVERY pad of the component at its new pose ({kind:'pad', ref, component, pin, net, position:{x_mm,y_mm}, layer, side, approach_sides, roles}), so where pin 1 landed is IN THIS REPLY and needs no follow-up minerva_pcb_pin_info call.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

snap_to_grid.description: Default true (2.54mm grid). false = FREEFORM: land EXACTLY at (x,y) — the way to do sub-grid pin alignment, e.g. straightening a 2-pin span whose pad rows sit off-grid relative to each other.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_move_relative
tools.description: Move a component using natural language direction (e.g., 'down a bit', 'closer to U3'). On success the reply may carry dangling_copper (same shape as minerva_pcb_move_component's). snap_to_grid:false lands exactly on the interpreted point instead of the 2.54mm grid. The reply's new_x/new_y are where the part actually LANDED; when the grid snap lands the part somewhere other than requested, the reply carries snapped:true + requested:[x,y] beside the landed coordinates — always read the reply's coordinates as the truth. On success the reply carries pads: [PAD ROW,...] — EVERY pad of the component at its new pose ({kind:'pad', ref, component, pin, net, position:{x_mm,y_mm}, layer, side, approach_sides, roles}), so where pin 1 landed is IN THIS REPLY and needs no follow-up minerva_pcb_pin_info call.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

direction.description: Natural language direction: 'up', 'down', 'left', 'right', 'closer to X', 'away from X', 'toward center', etc.

snap_to_grid.description: Default true. false = land exactly on the interpreted point (freeform).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_rotate_component
tools.description: Set a component's ABSOLUTE rotation in degrees — ANY angle, no snap (rotation is already freeform: 37.5 lands 37.5). The numeric value is the final orientation, NOT a delta: a component at 90 called with degrees:-90 lands at 270, not 0. For relative quarter turns pass the string 'clockwise' or 'counterclockwise' instead — these words mean what you SEE the part do on screen. Grouped components rotate their whole group as a rigid body about the group anchor. On success the reply may carry dangling_copper (same shape as minerva_pcb_move_component's) — copper does not follow parts. Requires editor_name from minerva_list_editors. ROTATION CONVENTION — the number and the words turn the part OPPOSITE ways, so read both. The NUMBER is KiCad's: rotation_deg applies as R(-angle) about the component origin in the board's y-down frame, which means a POSITIVE angle turns the part COUNTER-CLOCKWISE as drawn on screen. A pad sitting WEST of the origin therefore lands SOUTH at rotation 90 and NORTH at rotation 270; for a 2-pad part whose pad 1 is the west one, pin 1 ends up SOUTH at 90 and NORTH at 270. The WORDS are the screen's, not the number's: 'clockwise' turns the part a quarter turn clockwise as you watch it (rotation - 90) and 'counterclockwise' the other way (rotation + 90) — the same thing the panel's own rotate gesture and its R key do. On success the reply carries pads: [PAD ROW, ...] — EVERY pad of the component at its new pose ({kind:'pad', ref, component, pin, net, position:{x_mm,y_mm}, layer, side, approach_sides, roles}), so where pin 1 landed is IN THIS REPLY and needs no follow-up minerva_pcb_pin_info call.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

degrees.description: ABSOLUTE final rotation in degrees (0/90/180/270 or any angle) — NOT a delta. Negative values wrap mod 360 (-90 = 270).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_connect_net
tools.description: Move component pins onto a net (creates the net if it doesn't exist). A pin belongs to at most ONE net, so this MOVES: a pin already on another net is taken off that net in the SAME operation — there is no way to leave a pin on two nets, which would be a netlist short. The reply's `moved` array names every pin that changed net ({pin, from}) and is absent when nothing moved. The whole call is ONE undo step: minerva_pcb_undo restores every previous membership at once. Use minerva_pcb_disconnect_net to take a pin off its net without giving it a new one. Get pin names from minerva_pcb_describe_component first. Requires editor_name from minerva_list_editors.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

tools.name: minerva_pcb_disconnect_net
tools.description: Remove component pins from the net they are on — the removal half of minerva_pcb_connect_net. A pin belongs to at most one net, so `net_name` is OPTIONAL and is a GUARD, not a selector: give it to state which net you believe holds the pins and be refused (pin_not_on_net, naming the net each pin is actually on, nothing mutated) when that belief is stale, or omit it to take each pin off whatever net holds it. The whole call is ONE undo step. Returns {success, disconnected: [{pin, net}], not_connected?} where not_connected lists pins that were already on no net — not an error, they are already in the asked-for state. Requires editor_name from minerva_list_editors.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

net_name.description: Optional guard: the net you believe holds these pins. A pin on a different net refuses the whole call rather than being taken off a net you did not mean.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_free_pins
tools.description: What is AVAILABLE on a part: the pins of ONE component that are on NO net, as pad rows. This is the read behind "U1S.8/9 are on the east column but J2 is west — which free WEST pins can take I2C?": `side` filters to one side/COLUMN of the part (north | east | south | west, board frame, derived from the part's own pad geometry), so "the other side of U1S" is a filter rather than a coordinate scan. A part whose pins form exactly TWO COLUMNS reads those columns as west/east (and two rows as north/south) regardless of the part's aspect, so a WIDE 2x3 DIP answers side:"west" with all three of its west-column pins, not just the middle one. `exclude_roles` drops pins the BOARD's pin table flags — strapping, uart_console, jtag, onboard_led, adc — which is the owner's live filter for choosing a devkit GPIO. ROLES COME FROM THE BOARD, NEVER FROM MEMORY: a pin's canonical dict may carry `roles: [strapping]`, preserved verbatim through the document, and a board that declares nothing answers roles: [] rather than guessing which devkit this is. Returns {success, component_id, pin_count, free_count, free_pins:[PAD ROW], side?, excluded_roles?, note?} where a PAD ROW is the ONE shape minerva_pcb_get_selection and minerva_pcb_pin_info also use: {kind:'pad', ref, component, pin, net, position:{x_mm,y_mm}, layer, side, approach_sides, roles}. Read-only; journals nothing.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

component_id.description: The component whose free pins to list, e.g. "U1S"

side.description: Optional: keep only pads on this side/column of the part — north | east | south | west (board frame)

exclude_roles.description: Optional: drop pads carrying any of these roles, e.g. ["strapping", "uart_console", "onboard_led"]

tools.name: minerva_pcb_move_net
tools.description: MOVE one pin's net onto another pin, as ONE undo step — the verb twin of the pad selection's "Move net to…". The source pin comes OFF the net and the destination goes ON it: this is what "can we move these to the other side of U1S?" means once the target is chosen. A destination already on some other net is taken off it (a pin belongs to at most one net) and that is reported under `displaced` — the one fact you cannot read back afterwards. Pins are addressed as "Component.Pin", the same address minerva_pcb_get_selection returns for a selected pad. Returns {success, net_name, from, to, displaced?, pads:[PAD ROW, PAD ROW]} — the two pads AFTER the move, so no follow-up read is needed. Refuses by name and mutates nothing: same_pin, pin_not_found, pin_has_no_net (there is no net on the source to move — connect it first with minerva_pcb_connect_net).

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

from.description: Source pin as "Component.Pin" — the pin whose net moves away, e.g. "U1S.GPIO8"

to.description: Destination pin as "Component.Pin" — the pin that receives the net, e.g. "U1S.GPIO38"

tools.name: minerva_pcb_swap_nets
tools.description: EXCHANGE the nets of two pins, as ONE undo step — the verb twin of the pad selection's "Swap nets", and the BTN3/BTN4 correction the owner does by hand today. Each pin ends on the net the other was on. A pin on NO net is a legal side of the swap (the other pin's net moves to it and it gives nothing back); two netless pins have nothing to exchange. Pins are addressed as "Component.Pin". Returns {success, swapped:[{pin, was, now}, {pin, was, now}], pads:[PAD ROW, PAD ROW]} — the two pads AFTER the swap. Refuses by name and mutates nothing: same_pin, pin_not_found, nothing_to_swap, already_same_net.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_select
tools.description: SET the canvas selection for the human — the MIRROR of minerva_pcb_get_selection for a WHOLE selection, where minerva_pcb_point is the single-entity form. Use it to SHOW which pins or entities you mean instead of describing them: after the human says "see these pins? move them to the other side of U1S", answering with the candidate pads SELECTED is a reply they can look at. `pads` is the common case — a list of "Component.Pin" refs, the same addresses get_selection returns for selected pads. `entities` takes every other kind: [{kind, id}] with kind pad | component | trace | via | zone | cutout | candidate | staged | annotation. The selection is REPLACED: cleared once, then every entry lands through the same choke points a human click uses, so the canvas shows exactly what a click would have shown. Entries that no longer resolve are reported under not_found rather than failing the call. Returns {success, selected, not_found?, selection} where `selection` is minerva_pcb_get_selection's own read of the result — what this verb selected and what the deictic read reports cannot diverge.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_describe_region
tools.description: ONE read of everything the board has inside a rectangle — use this instead of stitching minerva_pcb_list_zones + minerva_pcb_describe_zone + minerva_pcb_get_components + minerva_pcb_spatial_query + minerva_pcb_pin_info together by hand when you need to understand the copper around a part. Read-only; journals nothing. x_mm/y_mm name the rectangle's TOP-LEFT corner, width_mm/height_mm its size (both must be > 0). Returns region_mm, layer, and: components[] {ref, position, rotation_deg, layer, pads[]} where each pad is THE pad row (ref "REF.PIN", component, pin, net, position, layer, side, approach_sides, roles) — the same shape minerva_pcb_get_selection and minerva_pcb_pin_info emit; traces[] {trace_id, net, layer, width_mm, points[], free_ends[], locked}, where free_ends names each end NOT joined to other copper, by the same rule the canvas Trace tool refuses to draw from and the connectivity DRC credits; vias[] {via_id, x_mm, y_mm, net_name, from_layer, to_layer, size_mm, drill_mm, layers_spanned[], layers_touched[]}; zones[] (copper pours) {zone_id, kind, net, layer, point_count, outline[], fill_region_count}; keepouts[] (same shape, no fill — a keepout emits no copper); cutouts[] {cutout_id, point_count, outline[]}; and notes[], the annotations whose ANCHOR POINT lies inside the rectangle. A trace crossing the boundary is listed WHOLE, with all of its points, because where a run goes is most of why you asked. fill_region_count 0 means the pour conducts NOTHING yet — an unfilled pour is a request for ground, not ground. layers_touched is which copper layers have copper actually MEETING the via's barrel, so a via that joins nothing on one side is visible without the tool judging it; layers_spanned is merely what the barrel passes through. An empty region returns empty arrays, never an error — the reply's `searched` list is what tells you an array is empty because nothing is there rather than because nothing was looked for. Optional `layer` filters everything that HAS a copper layer (traces, vias by span, zones, keepouts, pads) but never components, which are physical parts rather than copper on one layer. Copper is reported regardless of layer visibility: this answers what the BOARD has, not what the panel currently shows.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry
tools.description: Export routed traces and vias from a PCB editor. Returns trace data in the same format accepted by import_trace_geometry, enabling round-trip workflows. Every segment carries the trace_id of the trace it belongs to (the segments of one polyline trace all repeat the SAME trace_id — that is how you tell which segments are one piece of copper). Vias carry an id key when they have an identity, which is every via created through the editor or through import; the key is ABSENT on a via restored from a board file predating stable via ids, and such a via cannot be addressed by minerva_pcb_delete_traces. Use these ids with minerva_pcb_delete_traces to remove a subset, or feed them back through import_trace_geometry to keep identities stable across a round trip.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_cut_trace
tools.description: Cut ONE committed trace at an INTERIOR vertex: the trace keeps its id and its waypoints up to and including that vertex; the tail after it is dropped. The MCP twin of the canvas's right-click 'Cut here' on a trace, through the same model rule. Name the vertex by at_index (0-based into the trace's points; get them from minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry or the add_trace reply) OR by x_mm+y_mm, which picks the nearest interior vertex within the canvas's snap radius (1.27 mm) exactly as a click does. Exactly one journalled, undoable step. The new end is a free end unless something already joins it — reply free_end says which — and a free end can be continued by minerva_pcb_add_trace's start/end anchors. Refused by name, changing nothing: no_such_trace; trace_locked (a locked trace); no_vertex_in_reach (coordinate form found no interior vertex within snap); trace_not_cuttable (the model's own words — the index is an end, which would be a delete or a no-op, or the trace has fewer than 3 points). Reply {trace_id, at_index, kept_point_count, dropped_count, free_end, trace_count}. Runs no DRC.

at_index.description: 0-based index of the INTERIOR vertex to cut at (1 .. point_count-2). Use this or x_mm+y_mm.

x_mm.description: With y_mm: pick the nearest interior vertex within 1.27 mm of this point

tools.name: minerva_pcb_delete_traces
tools.description: Delete a SUBSET of committed traces and vias by identity, without touching the rest of the board. Use this instead of exporting everything, filtering, and re-importing (import_trace_geometry clears the whole board first). Get the ids from minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry, which stamps a trace_id on every segment and an id on every via. AT LEAST ONE of trace_ids, via_ids or net_name is REQUIRED — a call with none of them is an error, because deleting nothing and deleting everything must never be the same request. An EMPTY net_name (or empty id arrays) does not count as supplying a selector, so a call carrying only net_name:"" is that same error rather than a no-op. Selection is by identity ONLY — trace_ids, via_ids and net_name are combined as a union, and a trace named by both trace_ids and net_name is deleted and counted exactly once — and there is deliberately no region/bounding-box selector: to clear traces in an area, export, filter on the real coordinates yourself, then name the ids you chose. net_name selects traces only, never vias; name a via by id to remove it. Partial-trace clipping (splitting a trace at a boundary) is not supported — a trace is deleted whole or not at all. Naming an id that does not exist is NOT an error: the ids that do exist are deleted and the stale ones come back in missing_trace_ids/missing_via_ids. An EMPTY-string id is reported there too rather than skipped — that is what you get from an item predating stable ids, whose id key the export omits entirely. Those two keys are present only when you supplied the corresponding selector, so an empty array means 'checked, none stale' while an absent key means 'you named none'. Deleting copper that a COMMITTED route candidate owns retires that commit and REOPENS its routing task, so the workspace stops reporting that span as routed — the reply then carries reopened_candidate_ids (absent when no committed candidate was touched), and those candidates come back live, with any DRC verdict they held staled, to be re-checked or rerouted rather than re-committed blind over the copper that survived. Undoable in one step via the board's normal undo (the copper and the retired commit return together).

save_to_path.description: Optional absolute filesystem path to write the PNG to instead of returning it inline as base64. Parent directory must already exist. When set, the response omits image_data and instead returns {saved_to, width, height, byte_size} — read the file back with your file-read tool if you need to view it.

fit.description: Default true: frame the whole board (fit-to-content) before capturing, so a freshly-loaded board is never off-frame. Pass false to capture the CURRENT camera set by minerva_pcb_set_view (a zoomed-in detail).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_view_state
tools.description: Read — and optionally set — WHAT the PCB canvas is drawing, so you can interpret your own minerva_pcb_get_image instead of guessing. minerva_pcb_set_view aims the camera; this says what the camera is pointed at. Call with no arguments to read: returns {flags:{show_grid, show_traces, show_silk, show_ratsnest, show_labels, show_courtyard, show_route_candidates, show_drc_witnesses, show_mask, show_fab_preview}, layers:[{id, kicad, hidden}], trace_layer_filter, working_layer, changed:[]}. Writes are absolute, not deltas: flags {name:bool} sets any subset, and hidden_layers is THE COMPLETE set of canonical layer ids to hide (pass [] to show every layer, or every id but one to solo that layer — the way to inspect an inner layer on its own). Everything is validated before anything is applied, so a bad flag name or a layer this board does not declare changes nothing and names what was wrong. Toggling show_mask or show_fab_preview on runs the same worker refetch the View menu runs, so the overlay you then capture is real rather than empty. If that refetch comes back with nothing, the flag comes BACK DOWN — it may only claim a view that is actually on screen — so it reads false here and overlay_unavailable:{flag: reason} carries why, the same sentence the status bar shows the human. fab_preview_layer isolates ONE emitted Gerber/drill layer while the fab preview is up ("all", or a key from the fab_preview_layers list this call returns: "f_cu", "b_cu", "f_mask", "f_silks", "edge_cuts", "pth"…) — ten layers composited is a picture of no layer, and this is the same control the View menu gives the human. It is the one write validated AFTER it is applied, because its vocabulary is the artifact set the flags in this same call may have just fetched: a key the emitted set does not carry refuses with layer_not_emitted, lists what was emitted, and reports in changed whatever else already landed. trace_layer_filter is writable too ("all" or a declared copper layer id) and is applied LAST so an explicit value wins. The two compose ASYMMETRICALLY: a specific filter beats every per-layer eye, so applying hidden_layers resets the filter to "all" (reported in changed) — without that, soloing a layer would change the eyes and nothing on screen. SEPARATELY, and NOT a view control at all: working_layer is the copper the canvas AUTHORS on — the layer the toolbar chooser names and the trace tool, the zone tools and the bus draw on. Read it back on every call; write it with a declared copper layer id (never "all") to aim the human-facing tools. It composes with nothing above it: setting it changes nothing on screen, and no view write moves it. Direct authoring verbs (add_trace, create_zone, route_bus_direct) keep their own explicit layer args and ignore it.

flags.description: Any subset of the View draw flags, as {flag_name: bool}. Unknown names are refused by name and change nothing.

hidden_layers.description: THE COMPLETE set of canonical layer ids to hide ("top", "bottom", "in1"...). Absolute, not a delta: layers omitted here become visible. Omit the key entirely to leave layer visibility untouched.

trace_layer_filter.description: VIEW filter: "all", or a declared copper layer id to scope the whole view to that one layer. A specific value outranks every per-layer eye, so it is applied LAST. Does NOT change where copper is authored — that is working_layer.

fab_preview_layer.description: Which emitted layer the exact fab preview shows ON ITS OWN: "all", or a key from the fab_preview_layers list this tool returns ("f_cu", "b_silks", "edge_cuts", "pth"…). Only meaningful while show_fab_preview is up and holding artwork; a key the emitted set does not carry is refused by name.

Returns {view:{zoom, center_x_mm, center_y_mm, visible:{x_mm,y_mm,width_mm,height_mm}}} — the camera you ended up with, so you can see whether the board actually landed in frame.

center_x_mm.description: View centre X in board mm.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints
tools.description: Route the board's open route hints and either PROPOSE routes (default) or COMMIT them as real traces. Default (commit absent/false): runs the router over the selected open route hints and lands the results as RouteCandidates in the panel's routing workspace (no annotation is written; the board is not mutated) — resolve a candidate via minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/_reject(candidate_id), or minerva_pcb_workspace_list/get_active to inspect it first. Set commit=true to materialize the routed polylines as real traces in the board model (journaled) and transition the source hints open→applied. Partial/failed routing returns WHERE it got stuck (unrouted nets with their blocked pad pairs) as structured feedback, and every routing reply carries board_health: whole-board completeness + assembly advisory, enriched panel-side with board_revision and preflight.rendered_this_revision. ISLAND DELTA: island_deltas?:[{net, pin_groups_before, pin_groups_after, hint_ids?}] reports what each route BUYS against the pre-proposal census — e.g. 9 pin groups -> 8 means this candidate merges two islands; a delta of zero on a partial net means the new copper connects nothing new. ROUTE QUALITY: every candidate record carries bend_count and routed_length_mm (zeros for a vias-only candidate), plus length_ratio (routed / per-run manhattan minimum, approximate; absent when that minimum is ~0) and, on single-run candidates, misalignment_mm — the perpendicular offset between the span's endpoints (min(|dx|,|dy|)). THE 2-PIN RULE: on a two-pin span, ANY bend means the pads do not align — length_ratio 1.0 only says the detour is efficient, never that it is necessary; misalignment_mm > 0 says the PLACEMENT is the thing to fix (align with minerva_pcb_move_component snap_to_grid:false, then re-propose) — weigh that before committing. A high ratio or bend count on a longer hop is the same smell at larger scale. Iterate: edit/add hints and re-run; applied hints are excluded by default so only fresh open hints re-route. LAYER-HOP WAYPOINTS: a route hint's kind_payload.waypoints entry may be {"x": mm, "y": mm, "layer": "top"|"bottom"|"in1"..|a KiCad copper name} instead of [x_mm, y_mm], and that layer means THE RUN CHANGES TO IT HERE. The materializer ends the current run at that corner, places ONE through via there sized from the board's design_rules, and continues on the named layer — so ONE hint expresses "F.Cu, duck under here, back up there, F.Cu" and there are no orphan via ghosts for an agent to geometry-match. A waypoint with no layer key is an ordinary corner (absent means "stay on the layer you are on", never "default to top"); a waypoint restating the layer the run is already on is a corner too, not a hole. A hint whose waypoints carry layers takes the AS-DRAWN path whatever detail_level its waypoint count inferred, because naming where copper changes side is by construction drawing your own path. Refused by name and routed by the engine instead (with a warning naming the hint) when a waypoint layer is not copper or the board does not declare it. NOT honoured on the ENGINE path — a hint steered by a task corridor, or one setting allow_layer_change, hands every layer decision to the engine; the reply then warns that the authored hops were not placed rather than dropping them silently. LEGACY MIGRATION: a selected non-'detailed' hint carrying inline waypoints whose task has no routing_constraint yet has that corridor seeded ONCE into a durable task constraint (authored_by "migration") before routing runs, and the hint's waypoints are then marked superseded and refuse further edits. DRAFT-BOARD COMPOSITION: commit=false routes against the composed draft when placement ghosts are live — its proposals[] rows then carry draft_placements:[{id, component_id, to, status: satisfied|pending|invalidated}] (absent when no ghost was live at request composition), and the landed candidates cannot commit until every listed ghost is satisfied. commit=true always routes the REAL board, uncomposed. LAYER-CHANGE OPT-IN: a 'detailed' single-trace hint routes AS DRAWN — verbatim polyline, its one layer, no vias — unless its kind_payload sets allow_layer_change:true, which hands the drawn line to the engine as a corridor instead: the route follows the line but may break onto another copper layer through the normal costed via machinery. On an N-layer board (see minerva_pcb_set_board_layers) the engine routes every DECLARED copper plane; all vias are through-hole.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_undo

Replies with the label of the step reverted and how many steps remain in each direction. Refuses (nothing_to_undo) at the bottom of the history. Route-hint revisions have their own stack: use minerva_pcb_hint_undo for those.

tools.description: Redo the board history step most recently undone — the twin of Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y and the ribbon's Redo button. Replies with the label of the step re-applied and the remaining depth in each direction. Refuses (nothing_to_redo) when nothing was undone, or once a fresh edit has cleared the redo side.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_hint_convert_to_detailed
tools.description: Convert a SUPERSEDED guided route hint to 'detailed', reclaiming manual waypoint control. A legacy guided hint whose inline waypoints were seeded into a task-level routing constraint (marked kind_payload.waypoints_superseded_by_constraint_revision — the station-12 migration, or a live steer) has inert waypoints: the host refuses waypoint edits and routing reads only the constraint. This named operation clears that task constraint (only when this hint singly owns it), then strips the supersession marker and the offline lock fields and sets detail_level='detailed' — ordered two-store writes, NOT a spanning transaction: a torn save is repaired by deterministic load-time reconciliation, and undo restores the annotation side only (one history step; re-run this tool to complete a half-undone conversion) — afterwards the hint's waypoints are editable again, routing follows them literally (as-drawn) on the next propose, and the hint is never re-seeded. Use it when an edit was refused with error 'waypoints_superseded' (or offline with 'live_editor_required') and you want to hand-edit the path instead of steering the constraint. Refuses by name: constraint_not_singly_owned when a merged multi-hint task owns the constraint (converting would orphan shared steering — steer via minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route instead), not_superseded for an ordinary unstamped hint, hint_not_found / not_a_route_hint otherwise.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_via
tools.description: Manually insert a via on a pcb_route_hint proposal (a route carrying kind_payload.segments): splits the segment nearest board point (x, y) into two at the projected point, appends a via there, and recomputes every segment's copper layer via the layer-run toggle (F.Cu<->B.Cu at each via position, in path order) — the same split+via+layer-run geometry the canvas Add-Via tool uses, so an agent's call and a human's click produce identical results. Use this to resolve a routing collision by hand when the autorouter's own vias-avoidance left a proposal single-layer through an obstacle: one via jumps the trace to the opposite layer past that point, a second via jumps it back. No-op (error) if (x, y) is not near any segment. Persists through the host's revision-history seam, so minerva_pcb_hint_undo/minerva_pcb_hint_redo cover it.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_load_board
tools.description: Load a complete PCB board from canonical YAML into the editor in ONE call — components (with pins and pad geometry), nets, traces, vias, and mounting holes. This is the whole-board importer; it replaces the multi-call add_component / connect_net / import_footprint_geometry / import_trace_geometry sequence. Provide EXACTLY ONE of `path` (absolute file path, read server-side — PREFER THIS for files on disk: it costs ~20 tokens instead of the whole board twice) or `yaml` (inline canonical board source, for boards you authored in-context). The canonical contract: width_mm/height_mm, components[].ref whose pins carry pad geometry via drill_mm/annulus_diameter_mm for through-hole or pad_width_mm/pad_height_mm for SMD, plus nets, traces, vias, mounting_holes. Returns component_count, net_count, deserialize warnings, board_name, and source_digest (sha256 of the loaded YAML text — compare it to verify the board that landed is byte-identical to your source). DESTRUCTIVE REPLACE with an honesty report: loading swaps the WHOLE live board, and the reply's `delta` field names what the incoming source lacked relative to the live board it replaced (components_removed, traces_reduced per net, vias_removed, zones/cutouts/mounting_holes_removed, plus `dropped` sentences). READ IT — a source missing entities the live board had (e.g. a YAML with no zones) destroys them; reconciliation is the CALLER's judgment, this tool only reports. SIDECAR ADOPTION (Epoch UX2 station 8): the `path` form adopts the file as the panel's document path — annotations become durable-by-default (<path>.annotations.json auto-written debounced on every mutation), an existing sidecar (annotations + routing workspace) is restored on load, and the reply says so: annotations_sidecar:"adopted" + annotations_restored (count, when a sidecar was read). The inline `yaml` form adopts nothing. BOARD HEALTH AT LOAD (UX2 station 9): the reply carries `board_health` — the same whole-board ledger a route reply carries (completeness census: complete/missing_copper/partial/indeterminate, + tri-state assembly, panel-enriched with board_revision/preflight) — computed at open with NO routing run, so "8 nets unrouted, GND in 9 islands" is known before the first verb; the established `assembly` key remains.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_silk_text
tools.description: Render a string as silkscreen stroke geometry owned by the BOARD (not by a component). Args {editor_name, text, position:{x_mm,y_mm}, layer, size_mm, rotation_deg?, h_align?, width_mm?, id?}. size_mm is CAP HEIGHT: a capital is exactly that tall. B.SilkS text is MIRRORED automatically so it reads correctly once the board is flipped — a Gerber is plotted as seen from the top THROUGH the board, so back legend must be mirror-written in the file. The mirror is about the text's own anchor, so text asked for at (10,10) sits at (10,10) on either side: it reads the other way, it does not move. The board stores what the text SAYS, not its strokes, so fixing a typo is an edit to one string rather than a regeneration of a hundred polylines. Returns {graphic_id, layer, kind, text, size_mm, rotation_deg, mirrored, width_mm, bounds, missing_glyphs}. Characters with no glyph in the board font are drawn as a BOX and listed in missing_glyphs, never silently dropped. ONE undo step. Remove it with minerva_pcb_delete_graphic, or select it on the canvas and press Delete.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

text.description: The string to render. Printable ASCII is fully covered; any other character draws a box and is reported in missing_glyphs.

position.description: Anchor in board mm: the text baseline sits on y_mm, and x_mm is the left edge unless h_align is "center".

layer.description: Silk layer. B.SilkS mirrors the glyphs. Default "F.SilkS".

size_mm.description: Cap height in mm. Default 1.0, matching a reference designator.

rotation_deg.description: Rotation about the anchor, KiCad convention. Default 0.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_graphic
tools.description: Author raw stroke geometry owned by the BOARD on a silk or courtyard layer. Args {editor_name, layer, width_mm?, id?} plus EXACTLY ONE of: polylines (array of open point-chains), points (with closed:true for a closed polygon), rect:{start,end}, circle:{center,radius_mm}. Every point is {x_mm, y_mm} in board coordinates — the same shape zone and cutout outlines use, NOT the bare [x,y] pair component graphics ride with. Copper and Edge.Cuts are REFUSED: board-level copper would be unconnected metal with no net, and the board rim already has an owner (the profile and its cutouts). Returns {graphic_id, layer, kind, width_mm, bounds}, or {graphics:[...], graphic_count} when several polylines were supplied. ONE undo step for the whole call. Remove with minerva_pcb_delete_graphic.

Nothing is journalled and nothing appears on the board until minerva_pcb_staged_accept; the ghost persists via the routing sidecar without an explicit save. A staged keepout also detours DRAFT route proposals (the composed request). Reply: {entity_id, staged_id, kind, net, layer, point_count}.

tools.description: STAGE a cutout (an opening through the whole board) as a DRAFT — the staging family's twin of minerva_pcb_create_cutout (same args, same validation), landing a review ghost instead of writing the board. tools.name: minerva_pcb_propose_placement
tools.description: STAGE a component MOVE as a DRAFT — a ghost of the part at the proposed pose with a tether from its current position, for human review. FAMILY NOTE: propose_* tools STAGE BOARD ENTITIES; the unrelated workspace_propose_* tools run the ROUTER. The part does NOT move until minerva_pcb_staged_accept, and accepting NEVER touches copper — nets already routed to the part are FLAGGED in affected_nets (routed:true) and the human sees an amber tether; re-routing stays a separate, explicit act. The human can drag the ghost to counter-propose; read the current pose back via minerva_pcb_staged_list. Reply: {entity_id, staged_id, component_id, from, to, affected_nets, collisions?}. ROUTE PREVIEW (OFC-3): while the ghost is live, minerva_pcb_workspace_propose routes against the composed draft (component virtually at the ghost target), so the straight trace is visible beside the ghost before anyone accepts the move.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_staged_accept
tools.description: ACCEPT staged draft(s) (the staging family): replays the direct create with the STORED payload — same id, byte-identical entity — re-validated against the CURRENT board, so drift since staging (net deleted, layer removed) refuses with the direct verb's own reason and the draft stays live. One journalled history step; undo returns the entity to a ghost. Pass entity_id for one draft, or entity_ids (array) for an ALL-OR-NOTHING batch that lands as ONE undo step (refused whole, per-entity reasons, if any member cannot land). Copper is never auto-fixed (flag-don't-fix): delete or reroute is a separate act. Accepting a placement also DISCHARGES dependent route candidates: their draft_placements status flips to satisfied and workspace_commit stops refusing them.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_list_vias
tools.description: List every VIA on the board — the plated holes that carry a net from one copper layer to another. Read-only; journals nothing. Returns a via_count plus one entry per via: {via_id, x_mm, y_mm, net_name, from_layer, to_layer, size_mm, drill_mm, layers_spanned, layers_touched}. layers_spanned is what the barrel passes through (every through via spans the whole stack, so it says nothing about what the via joins); layers_touched is which of those layers have copper — a pad land, a trace, or a pour's compiled fill — actually MEETING the barrel, by the same contact rule the connectivity DRC reads. A via listing fewer touched layers than spanned joins nothing on the missing side; this NAMES that and judges nothing — whether it is a defect is minerva_pcb_drc's verdict to give. Use this to answer "which vias exist and where" without pulling the whole fabrication payload: minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry also carries a vias[] block, but that call walks every trace segment on the board and ABORTS entirely if any trace sits on a layer it cannot name, so an unrelated bad layer can make the via list unreadable. Both read the same board state, so the two never disagree. `via_id` is ABSENT (not blank) on a via restored from a board file predating stable via ids — such a via has no identity, so it cannot be deleted by id and cannot be selected on the canvas either. NOTE: minerva_pcb_add_via is NOT the counterpart of this tool — it edits a route-hint PROPOSAL, not the board, so nothing it adds appears here. Board vias are created by minerva_pcb_place_via (one via, directly — the counterpart this tool DOES have), by the canvas Via tool a human clicks, or by committing routes (minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints with commit, or minerva_pcb_import_trace_geometry); they are removed by minerva_pcb_delete_via or minerva_pcb_delete_traces' via_ids.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_trace
tools.description: Draw ONE trace directly on the board through the SAME model path the human's canvas Trace tool uses — the direct counterpart of minerva_pcb_delete_traces. Exactly one journalled, undoable step. Give net_name, layer ("top", "bottom", "in1"..., or a KiCad copper name) and points as [[x_mm,y_mm], ...] in order; width_mm is optional and falls back to the board's authored trace width. Returns {trace_id, net_name, layer, width_mm, point_count, segment_count, points, trace_count}. THIS RUNS NO DRC — the copper is on the board the moment it returns, exactly as the canvas Trace tool commits without gating, so run minerva_pcb_drc (connectivity) and minerva_pcb_drc_geometric (clearances) afterwards to find out what it touched. Refused by name, changing nothing: layer_not_on_stack (the board does not declare that layer — the reply lists the ones it does) and trace_not_authorable (the board model's own rule, e.g. too few points or an unknown net, reported in its own words so an agent and a human click are refused identically). To have a trace ROUTED for you around obstacles instead of drawn where you say, propose a route hint and apply it. TRACE-END ANCHORS: pass start and/or end as {trace_id, end: "start"|"end"} to CONTINUE an existing trace from a FREE end (one touching no pad, via or same-net copper), exactly as the canvas Trace tool does when clicked on one. A start anchor lends the run its net and layer (net_name/layer may then be omitted; if given they must agree); an end anchor must already share the run's net and layer. The trace is EXTENDED IN PLACE — same id, one journal row, one undo step — and the reply carries extended_from plus the whole grown polyline. Refusals: no_such_trace, trace_locked (a locked trace), trace_end_not_free (a joined end — also re-checked at the moment of the write), trace_end_same_trace (start and end name the two ends of one trace, which would close it into a loop), trace_end_net_mismatch, trace_end_layer_mismatch, trace_not_extendable.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_propose_via
tools.description: Propose ONE via as a GHOST for review — the Proposals-area twin of minerva_pcb_place_via. Nothing lands on the board until workspace_commit accepts it. Empty-space placement creates a standalone entity; if the via annulus physically reaches a trace, the target snaps to that trace's centreline, inherits its net (or refuses a conflicting supplied net), and Accept explicitly bisects the trace at the junction. Via-only boards remain valid. Args x_mm/y_mm, optional net_name, for_hint, size_mm, drill_mm. SIZE COMES FROM THE BOARD: omit size_mm/drill_mm and the via takes design_rules.via_diameter_mm / via_drill_mm (else 0.8 / 0.4) — the same rule the direct-commit paths use, so a ghost and the copper it becomes can never be different sizes; an explicit value still outranks the rules. OWNERSHIP — `for_hint` names the pcb_route_hint this via SERVES: the ghost records it on source_hint_ids, INHERITS that hint's net when net_name is omitted, and minerva_pcb_workspace_list shows the row as owner "hint <id>". Omit it and the via is still proposed (an unassigned via is legitimate) but every listing marks it owner "none" / unowned:true — nothing but its coordinates then says what it is for, which is exactly the state that made a human's four duck-under via ghosts un-attributable. Refuses hint_not_found / not_a_route_hint by name. On the canvas the same attribution happens by SELECTION: click the via with a route hint selected and the ghost is owned by it. Returns {candidate_id, via_id, x_mm, y_mm, net_name, trace_id, snapped_to_trace, size_mm, drill_mm, from_layer, to_layer, for_hint, owner}. A v1 via is THROUGH, so span arguments are refused. via_not_placeable covers ambiguous multi-net contact, net conflict, off-board/overlap/bad-ring placement, and stale trace context at commit. Human and MCP surfaces share the same resolver.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_fabrication_stage
tools.description: Read or DECLARE what this board is for manufacturing. Omit `stage` to read; pass it to declare. Returns {fabrication_stage, routing_deferred, known_stages, trace_count, via_count}. Stages: "routed" (the default, and what a board that declares nothing IS — every net is meant to be wired, today's behaviour exactly); "routing_deferred" (routing happens in a later step, some copper may already exist); "vias_only" (drilled and plated with no copper runs intended at all — the fiber-laser deliverable, where the customer cannot drill so they order the holes and lase the runs themselves). WHAT IT CHANGES: on a deferred board the connectivity census reports `complete:true` over a non-empty missing_copper, because unrouted nets are the JOB rather than a defect, and it carries fabrication_stage/routing_deferred/expected_incomplete beside the verdict so the reason always travels with it. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE: nothing is suppressed. Every unrouted and fragmented net is still computed and still listed, and the violation checks — shorts, crossings, dangling endpoints, layer changes with no via — fire exactly as before, because those report copper that is WRONG while a stage excuses only copper that is ABSENT. Refused by name, changing nothing: invalid_fabrication_stage (an unknown token, or "vias_only" on a board that has traces — that declaration would be false, so delete the traces or declare "routing_deferred"). One journalled, undoable step. The Properties sidebar's Fabrication row is the same declaration.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_update_via
tools.description: Edit ONE placed via — position, net, size or drill — in exactly one journalled, undoable step, keeping its id. The agent counterpart of dragging a via on the canvas or editing it in the Properties panel; all three share PCBData.update_via, so a call and a click are refused identically. Every argument except via_id is OPTIONAL and an absent one means UNCHANGED, but x_mm and y_mm must be given together (a via moves as a point). Returns {via_id, x_mm, y_mm, net_name, size_mm, drill_mm, trace_ids, snapped_to_trace, changed, from_layer, to_layer} — the RESULTING values, not the requested ones, because the edit is resolved against the board's copper: growing a via until its annulus reaches a trace snaps it to that centreline and inherits the trace's net, and clearing the net of a via that sits on a trace re-inherits that net, since a hole in that copper is on that net whatever you asked for. `changed:false` with success is a no-op (the via already had those values); a refusal is success:false with a named error. The whole edit is validated before anything is applied, so a refusal leaves the via untouched. Refused by name: via_not_placeable (off the board, overlapping another via, drill not smaller than pad, undeclared net, ambiguous multi-net trace contact, or a net that conflicts with the trace it touches) and span_not_selectable (a v1 via is a THROUGH via joining every declared layer; which layer a TRACE continues on past it is the run's property, not the hole's).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_delete_via
tools.description: Delete ONE board via by id. Exactly one journalled, undoable step — a single undo puts the via back. Get the id from minerva_pcb_list_vias (or from the `id` on each via in minerva_pcb_export_trace_geometry). Returns {deleted, net_name, x_mm, y_mm, remaining_via_count}. To remove several vias at once (or vias together with traces) in a single undo step, use minerva_pcb_delete_traces with via_ids instead. The human's Delete key, trash button and eraser on the canvas remove vias through this same model path and the same undo history. tools.name: minerva_pcb_board_rules
tools.description: Read — and optionally set — the RULES this board is drawn under: the directions its traces may run in, the four numeric design rules, the drawing-grid pitch, and the per-user toggles (three snaps plus hover_card, reported under snaps/view). This is the verb twin of the panel's own Options menu (the control strip's second menu, beside View); both call ONE shared read/write, so a human's click and this call are the same operation rather than two implementations that agree today. Call with nothing but editor_name to read: returns {trace_angle_mode, allowed_trace_angles_deg, offered_modes, design_rules:{trace_width_mm, clearance_mm, via_diameter_mm, via_drill_mm, grid_mm}, snaps:{snap_grid, snap_land, snap_angle}, changed:[]}. A design rule reading 0.0 means THE BOARD DECLARES NONE, which is a different fact from an authored 0.25 — so a caller can tell a rule from a fallback without guessing. TRACE ANGLES ARE A BOARD RULE, not a view flag: the set is written to design_rules.allowed_trace_angles_deg, travels with the YAML, snaps the Trace tool while a human draws, and is enforced on every trace by the worker's gc12_trace_direction check — agent-routed copper included. Entries are directions measured from +X toward +Y in the board's OWN y-down millimetre frame (so on screen the angle sweeps clockwise and 45 is the down-and-right diagonal), folded into [0, 180) because a direction and its reverse are one constraint. trace_angle_mode is the named shorthand: "manhattan" ([0, 90]), "octilinear" ([0, 45, 90, 135], the default a new board is created with) or "free" (the key is REMOVED, which is how "no direction constraint" is spelled everywhere in this stack). Pass trace_angle_mode OR allowed_trace_angles_deg, never both — a mode IS an angle set, and two spellings of one rule could disagree. A board declaring some other set reads back as mode "custom" and is never coerced to the nearest named one. Writes are VALIDATED WHOLE, THEN APPLIED WHOLE, the discipline minerva_pcb_view_state uses: an unknown mode, an unrecognised key, a malformed angle list or an out-of-range millimetre value changes NOTHING at all and names what was wrong (a misspelled key is refused by name, never silently ignored). Every board rule that really moved is listed in changed, and the board half of the write is exactly ONE undo step however many rules moved. The three snap toggles are PER-USER preferences and not board state (they persist in the same plugin preference store minerva_pcb_get_preference reads): how eagerly a cursor is pulled is a habit of the person drawing, while what it is pulled onto belongs to the board. snap_land governs FINISHING a run on a pad, via or free trace end; STARTING one always uses the land under the cursor, because that is where the run's net comes from.
