tools.name: minerva_pcb_set_refdes
tools.description: Read — and optionally move — WHERE a component prints its reference designator ("R1", "U3") on silkscreen. Call with nothing but editor_name and component_id to read: returns {component_id, ref, anchor:{x_mm, y_mm, rotation_deg, size_mm, hidden}, bounds:{min_x_mm, min_y_mm, max_x_mm, max_y_mm, width_mm, height_mm}, changed:[]}. THE ANCHOR IS FOOTPRINT-LOCAL millimetres in the part's own frame, y-down, and it is the text BASELINE, centred horizontally — the glyphs grow UPWARD from it, so a y_mm of -2.8 puts the label above the part. It rotates and mirrors with the component, so a part flipped to the back keeps its label in the same place relative to its own body. BOUNDS is the answer in the BOARD frame: the box the designator strokes actually occupy after that placement, so a caller that just moved a label can see where it landed without redoing the transform (empty when the designator draws nothing — hidden, or an unnamed part). WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM: minerva_pcb_drc_geometric reports gc9_silk_under_part and gc9_silk_over_silk advisories for legend that will be unreadable on the assembled board, and each of those rows carries a `suggestion` in exactly this argument shape — pass it straight back here. A suggestion of hidden:true means no position around the part is clear. Writes are VALIDATED WHOLE, THEN APPLIED WHOLE, the discipline minerva_pcb_view_state and minerva_pcb_board_rules use: a misspelled key, a non-finite number, a size_mm outside 0.2-10 mm (cap height, NEVER clamped) or a footprint-local offset past +/-500 mm changes NOTHING at all and is refused by name. Every field that really moved is listed in changed, and a write that lands is exactly ONE undo step. hidden:true prints no designator for this component at all, matching the emitter's rule for a footprint whose reference is authored hidden. WHAT YOU SET IS WHAT THE FAB PRINTS: the placement becomes AUTHORED BOARD STATE (the component's `refdes_placement` key), so it is written into the board file, the YAML export and the promote, and it outranks both the footprint's own reference fp_text and the derived default on every consumer — the Gerber F.SilkS designator, the DRC silk projection and the .kicad_pcb reference all move with it. Requires editor_name from minerva_list_editors.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

component_id.description: Component ID whose designator anchor to read or move

x_mm.description: Footprint-local x of the text anchor, mm. The designator is centred horizontally on it.

y_mm.description: Footprint-local y of the text BASELINE, mm, board y-down. Glyphs grow upward from the baseline, so a negative value puts the label above the part.

rotation_deg.description: Text rotation within the footprint frame, degrees.

size_mm.description: Cap height in mm. Must be between 0.2 and 10 — an out-of-range value is refused by name, never clamped.

hidden.description: True prints no designator for this component at all.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_get_preference
tools.description: Read one PCB plugin preference. Plugin-scoped and persistent across app restarts; NOT a Minerva core preference. Returns {key, value, stored, default, description} plus min/max where the key is bounded — `stored` distinguishes "the user/agent actually chose this" from "never chosen, reading the default", which is what decides whether the preference is consulted at all. Read-only: journals nothing, writes nothing. An unknown key is an error that lists the keys that do exist. Known keys: trace_width_mm, snap_grid, snap_land, snap_angle. The BOARD's own design rules are not preferences — read those with minerva_pcb_board_rules.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

key.description: Preference key to read (trace_width_mm, snap_grid, snap_land, snap_angle)

tools.name: minerva_pcb_set_preference
tools.description: Write one PCB plugin preference. Plugin-scoped, persisted under the plugin's data directory, survives app restart; NOT a Minerva core preference. The value is validated and CLAMPED to the key's declared range (unlike minerva_pcb_set_trace_width, which refuses out-of-range widths because it writes copper) and the reply reports the stored post-clamp value with {clamped, changed, applied_to_panel}. An unknown key is refused, never silently adopted. Known keys: trace_width_mm (a number) plus the toggles snap_grid, snap_land, snap_angle and hover_card (true/false), which the panel's Options menu turns and the canvas re-reads live. A boolean is validated and never clamped — there is no range to clamp into. Setting trace_width_mm updates the live panel's trace-width box immediately and arms it for the next trace drawn. The arming is IMMEDIATE: the next trace drawn uses this width even on a board declaring design_rules.trace_width_mm. Board-rule precedence applies at seeding time only — on the next board load the declared rule wins again and the preference fills the no-rule case.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab

key.description: Preference key to write (trace_width_mm, snap_grid, snap_land, snap_angle)

value.description: New value. For trace_width_mm: width in mm, clamped into 0.1-5.0. For a snap toggle: true or false.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_validate
tools.description: Structurally validate a canonical PCB board (board-yaml contract). Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Returns {ok, errors:[{path,message}], warnings:[...]} — errors flag structural faults (missing required fields, duplicate refs, net pin refs that don't resolve, traces on unknown nets); warnings flag soft issues (out-of-bounds coordinates, trace narrower than design rules). Cheap: no geometry engine.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_generate
tools.description: Generate KiCad files from a canonical PCB board. Args {yaml|board, name?:<basename>, out_dir?:<dir>}. Returns {files:{'<name>.kicad_pcb':text, '<name>.kicad_sch':text, '<name>.kicad_pro':text}, written:[{path,bytes_written}]}. The .kicad_pcb faithfully carries components/pads/traces/outline/vias at the authored coordinates; .kicad_sch/.kicad_pro are minimal netlist-carrying skeletons. When out_dir is given the files are also written to disk.

name.description: Optional output file basename (defaults to board name).

out_dir.description: Optional directory to also write the files to.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_gerbers
tools.description: Generate fabrication files (Gerber RS-274X/X2 + Excellon drills) from a canonical PCB board — pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml|board, name?:<basename>, out_dir?:<dir>}. Returns {files:{'<name>-F_Cu.gbr':text, ...}, written:[{path,bytes_written}], warnings:[...]}. NINE Gerber layers — F_Cu/B_Cu, F_Mask/B_Mask, F_Paste/B_Paste, F_SilkS/B_SilkS and Edge_Cuts — plus separate plated (PTH) and non-plated (NPTH) Excellon drill files (each drill file only when the board has holes of that class) and a '<name>-job.gbrjob' naming every layer's function. Coordinate format is self-declared per layer (read the %FS line, not assume 4.6). Silk is REAL footprint legend geometry plus stroke-font reference designators, on BOTH sides. Fab-correctness still needs a human viewer check — see docs/gerbers.md.

name.description: Optional output file basename (defaults to board name).

out_dir.description: Optional directory to also write the files to.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_drc
tools.description: Run a CONNECTIVITY/topology check over a canonical PCB board (pad centers + trace centerlines; NOT a geometric copper DRC — use minerva_pcb_drc_geometric for copper clearance/width/annular). Pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Holding an editor? Use minerva_pcb_board_drc {editor_name} — it checks the LIVE board in place with no export round-trip. Returns {ok, findings:[{type,...}], counts:{type:count}}. Findings are structured and located: 'wrong_net_pad' (a trace endpoint on, or a segment passing over, a different-net pad -> short) {net, at:[x,y], pad:{ref,pin,net}}; 'crossing' (two same-layer different-net traces that intersect, deduped per net-pair-per-layer) {nets:[a,b], layer, at}; 'dangling_endpoint' (a leaf trace endpoint reaching no pad/via/same-net copper -> open) {net, at}; 'layer_change_no_via' (a net's top and bottom copper meet with no via or through-hole pad -> missing via) {net, at}. T-junction taps and same-component internal-net pads are credited so they don't read as false opens. Scope: checks key off trace endpoints/segments — this is NOT a full ratsnest/connectivity check; a pad with no trace routed near it is not flagged as unrouted.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_drc_geometric
tools.description: Run a GEOMETRIC copper design-rule check over the ResolvedBoard IR — real pad/trace/via/hole copper geometry, pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Holding an editor? Use minerva_pcb_board_drc {editor_name, geometric: true} — it checks the LIVE board in place with no export round-trip. Compiles the board to the ResolvedBoard IR, then checks GC1 min trace width, GC2 copper-copper clearance, GC3 drill/finished-hole (finished-hole is a necessary pre-DFM check — the IR carries drill diameter, not the plated finished bore), GC4 annular ring, GC5 copper-to-edge, GC6 hole-to-hole, GC7 filled-pour clearance, GC8 solder-mask sliver, GC10 hole-to-copper, and GC11 hole-to-edge (an unconditional containment refusal for a bore that crosses the outline or enters a cutout, plus a proximity check that runs only when the profile declares min_hole_to_edge_mm). GC9 silkscreen is ADVISORY in BOTH its halves: DFM (legend stroke width, legend-to-pad) and PLACEMENT — `gc9_silk_under_part` for legend printed inside a foreign component's keep-out envelope, or a designator inside its own part's body/pad extent, and `gc9_silk_over_silk` for a designator crossing another part's designator or outline or board-level silk. A footprint's own outline sitting inside its OWN courtyard is never a row — that is the footprint convention. Every designator row carries `suggestion` {x_mm, y_mm, rotation_deg, size_mm, hidden} — exactly the argument shape minerva_pcb_set_refdes takes, so it can be passed straight back unedited — beside a row-level `suggested_slot`: the compass slot the suggestion came from (N, S, E, W, then the diagonals), or null when no slot clears and the suggestion is hidden:true. The slot chosen is the first at the footprint's own derived offset that clears both placement rules and the silk-to-pad floor. Advisory rows appear in a separate top-level `advisories` array and are counted, but are NOT in `findings` and NEVER change `verdict` — legend is cosmetic and is warned, never fatal. Floors declared OPTIONAL by a profile (hole-to-copper, hole-to-edge, the silk pair, feature-specific drill minima) are enforced only when that profile states them. `counts` reports ROWS, not check coverage: zero can mean either 'the profile stated no floor' or 'the check ran and found no row'. A GC9 failure is explicit as a counted `gc9_silk_indeterminate` advisory, never inferred from the two measuring counts. NEVER a false clean: modeled copper is exact or a superset (fail-safe), and unresolved/unsupported geometry FAILS CLOSED to an indeterminate result. Returns a discriminated union — determinate {ok:true, scope:'geometric', verifies_geometry:true, verdict:'clean'|'violations', board_id, source_digest, rule_profile, findings:[{type, entity_id, net_id, layer, measured_mm, required_mm, witness}], advisories:[...same shape...], counts, not_evaluated:[{check, floor, reason, scope?}], static_warnings:{rows:[{code, count, severity, message, refs, refs_omitted?}], digest, total}} or indeterminate {ok:false, verdict:'indeterminate', error:{kind}} with NO clean/findings. `not_evaluated` names every rule whose floor the selected profile (or the board, for gc12_trace_direction) does not declare, so a zero count that means NOT MEASURED can be told from one that means clean. `static_warnings` collapses the per-entity compile warnings into one row per code with a digest that is stable across identical calls; pass verbose_warnings:true to get the flat `warnings` list beside it. Distinct from minerva_pcb_drc (connectivity/topology only). Corroborated against kicad-cli DRC.

verbose_warnings.description: Return the FLAT per-entity compile warnings beside the grouped static_warnings (default false). The flat list is dozens of rows saying the same thing about different entities, unchanged between runs and re-sent on every call; the grouped form carries a digest that moves the moment any warning does.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_board_drc
tools.description: The LIVE-BOARD form of the two DRC verbs: check the board that is open in the named PCB editor, in place. No export, no file, no parse — the panel snapshots the live board and sends it to the same worker check minerva_pcb_drc / minerva_pcb_drc_geometric run, by reference when the board is over the MCP/broker cap (the smart-remote class), so a board of any size is one call. geometric:false (default) runs the connectivity/topology check (minerva_pcb_drc's findings + counts); geometric:true runs the geometric copper DRC (minerva_pcb_drc_geometric's union: verdict, findings, advisories, counts, not_evaluated, static_warnings; verbose_warnings as there). The reply is FINDINGS ONLY plus check ('connectivity'|'geometric') and board_source:'editor' — the board is never echoed. Use the two document verbs when you hold yaml/board and no editor.

editor_name.description: Name of the PCB editor tab whose live board is checked

geometric.description: true: run the geometric copper DRC (minerva_pcb_drc_geometric); false/omitted: the connectivity/topology check (minerva_pcb_drc).

verbose_warnings.description: geometric only: return the FLAT per-entity compile warnings beside the grouped static_warnings (default false).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_resolve
tools.description: Enrich a canonical PCB board with footprint silkscreen + courtyard graphics — pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. For each component the footprint ref is resolved from the sha-verified seed library and its F.SilkS body outline + F.CrtYd keep-out graphics are attached as component['graphics'] (component-LOCAL coords; the placement/rotation transform stays the renderer's job, like pins). The existing inline pads are left untouched. FAIL-CLOSED coincidence guard: every declared pin's local position must equal the footprint pad's local position (matched by number) within 0.01mm, else {ok:false, error:{kind:'coincidence', ref, pin, delta_mm}} — never attach silk that would desync from the routed copper. Returns {ok, board:<resolved board>, stats:{components, silk_graphics, courtyard_graphics}}.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_normalize
tools.description: Rewrite a canonical PCB board to its normalized v2 shape — the sync-back the compile fold never persists on its own. Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. For every pin carrying deprecated inline fabrication geometry (drill_mm/annulus_diameter_mm/pad_width_mm/pad_height_mm/plated): geometry REDUNDANT with the locked footprint pad is dropped, geometry that DIVERGES is migrated to a typed `override`, and an AMBIGUOUS pin (no matching footprint pad, or unverifiable) fail-closes the WHOLE normalize (better none than a half-normalized source). PURE — returns the normalized board for the host to persist; never writes to disk. Returns {ok:true, board:<normalized>, warnings:[{severity,code,message,...}]} on success (the warnings carry per-pin migrate/drop INFO diagnostics), or {ok:false, error:{kind:'normalize'|'parse', message, diagnostics}} on a fail-closed or parse fault. Idempotent: normalizing an already-normalized board is a no-op.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_lock_libraries
tools.description: PIN a PCB board to the library content it currently resolves, so a rebuild months later reproduces the same copper or REFUSES (acceptance check K20). Args {yaml:<board source>} or {board:<board object>}. Component.footprint is a NAME, and a user library layer may legitimately override a seed part under the same name — so without a lock the same board can resolve to different geometry later with nothing saying so. This records, per footprint the board actually uses, the sha256 of the content that resolved plus the layer that supplied it; a later compile refuses by name when the sha no longer matches. PURE — returns the locked board for the host to persist; never writes to disk. Relocking REPLACES the block rather than merging, so a pin for a part the board no longer uses cannot survive forever. Returns {ok:true, board:<locked>, locked:[refs], unresolved:[{ref,reason}]}; `unresolved` names any footprint no layer supplies — those cannot be pinned, and a caller that ignored it would believe the board fully pinned when part of it is not.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_check_libraries
tools.description: Verify component footprints against KiCAD footprint-library data. Args {yaml|board, lib_dir?:<path to a dir of *.pretty libs>}. With no lib_dir (the library data ships with a later child) returns {ok:true, checked:0, missing_data:true} — never a crash. With lib_dir returns {ok, checked, missing:[{ref,footprint,path}], missing_data:false}.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_check_bom
tools.description: Extract + validate a bill of materials from a canonical PCB board. Args {yaml|board, lib_dir?}. Returns {ok, items:[{refs,footprint,value,qty}], line_count, part_count, errors, warnings}. Warns on components missing a value or footprint. Footprint-presence flags are added only when lib_dir is supplied.

lib_dir.description: Optional KiCAD footprint-library dir for presence checks.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_stage
tools.description: Stage a .kicad_mod footprint into the WIP library layer, sha256-pinned and UNBLESSED. Args {ref:'LibNick:PartName', kicad_mod_text, source_kind:'official_kicad|vendor_export|git|url|hand_authored|generated', source_ref, license, retrieved_at?, provenance_note?}. Returns {ref, entry:<acquisition-lock v2 entry with bless:null>, report:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}}. The text is PARSED FIRST — unparseable or padless input writes no file and mutates no lock. A staged entry cannot supply copper until minerva_pcb_footprint_bless records a verdict against it: unblessed refs are excluded from the resolution chain, so a board resolves the lower layer's part rather than the staged bytes. Re-staging a ref replaces its bytes and RESETS bless to null. Empty source_kind/source_ref/license are refused by name.

ref.description: Full footprint ref, 'LibNick:PartName' — the library nickname names the .pretty directory the staged file is written into.

kicad_mod_text.description: The complete .kicad_mod s-expression text to stage.

source_kind.description: Provenance class: official_kicad, vendor_export, git, url, hand_authored or generated.

source_ref.description: Where the bytes came from (URL, git rev, datasheet + author, ...).

license.description: SPDX id or LicenseRef for the staged text.

provenance_note.description: Optional free-text note kept on the lock entry.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_report
tools.description: Render the two artifacts a human blesses a footprint against: a FACT TABLE and a self-contained SVG. Args {ref, max_svg_bytes?}. Returns {ref, facts:{ref, footprint_name, layer, source_kind, license, source_ref, pad_count, pad_numbers, pads:[{number,type,shape,x_mm,y_mm,size,drill,drill_shape,drill_size,layers,rotation,roundrect_rratio,solder_mask_margin,solder_paste_margin}], courtyard_bbox, body_bbox, assembly}, not_rendered:[{feature,detail,...}], svg, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256, svg_bytes, svg_truncated}. artifact_sha256 digests the staged content sha + the complete facts + not_rendered + the picture — it is what a human-tier bless must quote back as expected_artifact_sha256. Coordinates in facts are footprint-LOCAL with KiCad's y-DOWN sign (verbatim from the .kicad_mod); the SVG negates y so the picture is a conventional top view, and does not mirror x, so back-side geometry is drawn as seen through the board. not_rendered lists EVERY parsed element the picture omits — an empty not_rendered is the only condition under which the render shows the whole part. svg_sha256/svg_bytes always describe the WHOLE artifact even when svg itself is truncated for transport.

ref.description: Footprint ref to report on ('LibNick:PartName'); resolves through the layer chain, staged WIP parts included.

max_svg_bytes.description: Truncate the returned svg body at this many bytes (default 200000). svg_sha256/svg_bytes still describe the whole artifact.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_bless
tools.description: Record a bless verdict against a staged footprint, which is what lets it supply copper. Args {ref, verdict?:'approved'|'rejected', who?, blessed_at?, expected_artifact_sha256?}. Returns {ref, entry:<entry with bless:{tier, verdict, who, artifact_sha256, content_sha256, blessed_at}>, report:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}}. TIERING: source_kind official_kicad AUTO-BLESSES on provenance — omit verdict for it, and passing one is refused rather than silently recorded, so the lock can always distinguish parts a human reviewed from parts policy trusted. Every other source_kind (hand_authored above all — we authored those numbers) requires an explicit human verdict PLUS expected_artifact_sha256: the artifact_sha256 of the minerva_pcb_footprint_report the reviewer actually looked at. If the staged content changed since that review the bless REFUSES — an approval never transfers to an artifact nobody saw. The render is regenerated here and its digest pinned, so a footprint that cannot be rendered cannot be blessed. A 'rejected' verdict is recorded and keeps the ref unresolvable.

verdict.description: 'approved' or 'rejected'. OMIT for an official_kicad entry, which auto-blesses; supplying one for it is refused.

who.description: Who performed the rendered check. Required for a human-tier verdict.

blessed_at.description: Timestamp to record (defaults to UTC now).

expected_artifact_sha256.description: artifact_sha256 of the report the reviewer looked at. Required with a human-tier verdict; the bless refuses if the staged content renders a different artifact now.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_acquire_footprint
tools.description: Acquire ONE official KiCad footprint by ref and make it usable in a single call. Args {ref:'LibNick:PartName'}. Performs outbound HTTPS to gitlab.com for the kicad-footprints file at the release tag pinned in pcb/libraries.lock.json (the lock is the single source of truth for which official release this plugin tracks — the tag is read, never restated here), then hands the bytes to the worker, which parse-validates them, stages them into the WIP library layer, and records the auto-tier verdict official_kicad provenance earns. Returns {ref, layer:'wip', sha256, source_ref:'kicad-footprints@<tag>/<Lib>.pretty/<Name>.kicad_mod', license, bless:{tier:'auto', verdict, who, artifact_sha256, blessed_at}, entry, report_summary:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}} — the ref resolves immediately afterwards. Refuses without writing anything on: a ref with a path separator or traversal segment, a non-200 status (404 = no such part at this release), a body over 1 MiB, non-UTF-8 bytes, or content that is markup rather than a footprint s-expression. The sha256 of the fetched bytes is recomputed independently worker-side and a mismatch is refused. ACQUISITION is the only library operation that needs a network: resolution reads sha-pinned bytes off disk and never opens a socket, so a fetch failure blocks adding this part and nothing else.

ref.description: Official KiCad footprint ref, 'LibNick:PartName' (e.g. 'Resistor_SMD:R_0402_1005Metric') — the library nickname names the upstream .pretty directory.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_footprint_promote
tools.description: Promote a BLESSED footprint out of the WIP staging layer into the durable USER library layer, where every compile-bearing tool (gerbers, generate, drc, drc_geometric, resolve, route, ...) resolves it from then on. Args {ref:'LibNick:PartName', overwrite?:bool}. Returns {ref, layer:'user', path, entry} — the acquisition-lock entry moves WHOLE (bless record, provenance, assembly) with only its layer rewritten, and the WIP staging slot is freed. Refuses BEFORE any write: a ref that is not staged, staged but not blessed-approved (rejected or never reviewed), whose staged bytes no longer match the blessed sha256 pin, whose destination lock is not schema v2, or that already exists in the user library without overwrite:true. The WIP and user library roots are host-owned paths under the plugin data directory; the caller never chooses them.

ref.description: Full footprint ref, 'LibNick:PartName', of a staged AND blessed WIP entry.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing user-library entry of the same ref (default false: refused).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_import_footprint
tools.description: Import ONE footprint from an ARBITRARY source — a git repository at a pinned revision, a direct URL, or a vendor-export archive (SnapEDA, UltraLibrarian, a manufacturer download) already on this disk — and stage it for human review. Args {ref:'LibNick:PartName', source_kind:'git'|'url'|'vendor_export', license, git_url + git_rev + path_in_repo (git), url (url), archive_path (vendor_export), provenance_note?}. THE IMPORTED PART IS NEVER AUTO-BLESSED: it lands in the WIP layer with bless:null and cannot supply copper until minerva_pcb_footprint_report is looked at and minerva_pcb_footprint_bless records an explicit human verdict against its artifact_sha256 — unlike minerva_pcb_acquire_footprint, whose official_kicad provenance is the one thing this plugin trusts without a person. Returns {ref, layer:'wip', sha256, source_kind, source_ref, license, original_source_path, entry, report_summary:{facts, not_rendered, svg_sha256, artifact_sha256}}. The ORIGINAL source bytes are preserved verbatim under originals/<Lib>.pretty/<Part>/<source filename> in the WIP root — outside the resolvable layer, so it is insurance and never geometry — and source_ref records git+<url>@<rev>:<path>, url+<url>, or vendor_export+<archive>@sha256:<digest>!<entry>. Refuses without writing anything, each by name: a missing license (an entry that cannot say whose terms it carries), source_kind carrying another importer's fields, a git_rev that is not a full object id (a branch or tag is not a pin), a non-https URL, ANY redirect (not followed), a Content-Type other than text/plain or application/octet-stream, a body over 1 MiB, a zip entry whose path escapes the archive (zip-slip), a declared decompression ratio that is a zip bomb, and an archive holding zero or several .kicad_mod files (naming the count). The git clone is made with --no-checkout into a temporary directory under a replaced environment, so no repository-named path is ever materialised on disk.

ref.description: Full footprint ref, 'LibNick:PartName' — the library nickname names the .pretty directory the imported file is staged into.

source_kind.description: Which importer to run: 'git', 'url' or 'vendor_export'. Not free text — it selects the code path, and official_kicad is not importable here.

license.description: SPDX id or LicenseRef the imported text is under. Required: an entry with no license is refused before anything is fetched.

url.description: source_kind=url: the https URL of one .kicad_mod file. Redirects are refused, not followed.

git_url.description: source_kind=git: an https:// repository URL (or file:// for a repository already on this machine).

git_rev.description: source_kind=git: the FULL git object id (40 hex chars) to read at. A branch or tag name is refused — it is not a pin.

path_in_repo.description: source_kind=git: repository-relative path to the .kicad_mod, e.g. 'footprints/MyLib.pretty/Part.kicad_mod'.

archive_path.description: source_kind=vendor_export: absolute path to a .zip already downloaded to this machine. It must contain exactly one .kicad_mod.

provenance_note.description: Optional free-text note kept on the lock entry (datasheet revision, who downloaded it, why this source).

tools.name: minerva_pcb_export_assembly
tools.description: Generate a pre-assembly order package (BOM CSV + CPL/pick-and-place CSV) from a canonical PCB board for one assembly house profile — pure Python, no KiCad binary. Args {yaml|board, profile?:<house id, default "jlc">, name?:<basename>, out_dir?:<dir>}. "jlc" is the only house profile that currently offers assembly service; "oshpark" is a KNOWN house that refuses (bare-board only — no assembly service). Returns {profile, bom:{filename,rows,path}, cpl:{filename,rows,path}} — rows counts data rows (header excluded); path is omitted unless out_dir was given, in which case both CSVs are also written to disk. Refusals are NAMED, never a silent best-guess format or a blank identity cell: a component the profile requires identity for (jlc requires mpn) and lacks it refuses naming the component ref; an unrecognized or assembly-incapable house id refuses naming the id. Both CSVs are derived from ONE strict compilation of the board — the same compilation the gerbers come from — so a board that does not compile yields NO BOM and NO CPL: that refuses as kind "assembly_not_compilable" with a blocked_by list naming every component/footprint that stopped the compile. CPL coordinates are the resolved ASSEMBLY ANCHOR — the part's body-box centre, not the footprint origin x_mm/y_mm place — with Y negated and X verbatim, unmirrored on the bottom side; rotation is the composed placement angle, which reads as JLCPCB's counter-clockwise-positive convention in the emitted frame. A component authoring assembly.placements expands into one BOM quantity and one CPL row per authored placement, its offset composed against the parent's rotation and side; each expanded part inherits the anchor measured off the parent footprint unless its placement authors its own anchor_mm (the part's own body centre in that placement's frame), which a drawing standing for several parts spread across it must do — the parent's body centre is then the centre of none of them, and the anchor pass records basis "authored" for a placement that answered. HARD GATES run before either file is rendered and each refuses with a stable code naming the component and the field: assembly_duplicate_designator (a designator repeated, or repeated only after case-folding), assembly_reference_set_mismatch (BOM and CPL naming different designators), assembly_row_ref_limit (a grouped BOM row over the profile's max_refs_per_row), assembly_placements_too_close (two designators on one side under the profile's min_designator_separation_mm — usually a synthetic expansion with a zero offset), assembly_empty_expansion (assembly.placements authored but naming none), assembly_paste_undecided (a not-populated part whose lands take solder paste with assembly.paste still "auto" — author include or exclude), assembly_missing_identity, and assembly_non_metric_coordinates. A do-not-populate part keeps its copper, mask and drill in the gerbers, leaves BOTH CSVs, and is listed in excluded_components; assembly.paste: exclude additionally drops its stencil apertures. ADVISORIES do not refuse: advisories[] carries findings the caller should show, today assembly_anchor_unmeasured — a populated part whose footprint draws neither a fab body outline nor a sized land, so the emitted coordinate is its drawn origin rather than a measured centre. Both lists are absent when empty. The BOM's Comment column is assembly.comment (falling back to the component's value), its Footprint column is assembly.package (falling back to the authored footprint ref), and its part-number column is assembly.house_parts entry for the selected house (falling back to assembly.mpn) — so a board carrying two houses' catalogue numbers ships the selected house's. Calls the worker's assembly_package method ONCE: both CSVs come from one compilation and one walk, which is what makes them describe the same board.

Downloads each locked entry, verifies it by sha256, and skips entries already present+verified (safe to re-run). Args: none. Returns {tag, fetched:[names], skipped:[names], failed:[{name,reason}]}. tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_propose
tools.description: Route the open route hints into the ROUTING WORKSPACE as candidates (ghost routes), writing no proposal annotations. The workspace-native replacement for minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints' propose half: candidates carry exact per-segment layers/widths and vias, stable ids, and a disposition (proposed/pinned/superseded/rejected/committed) you act on with the other minerva_pcb_workspace_* verbs. Args {editor_name, hint_ids?, spans?}. WIDTH: a candidate on a net that ALREADY carries copper is proposed at that net's own established width (its widest existing trace) and reports width_source "net_copper" — never the board default, which would silently under-size a span joining wide power copper. A net with no copper yet takes the board default ("board_rules"); a hint width or an explicit option still outranks both and says so. SPANS: spans:[{source_pin, dest_pin, width_mm?, note?, corridor?}] mints the route intent per span internally (same validation, annotation, citeable ref, and width channel as minerva_pcb_add_route_intent — atomic across both stores: any invalid span refuses before anything mints or routes), then routes the minted hints in THIS call; spans + hint_ids are a UNION in one worker run, and the reply carries minted_hint_ids naming the intents created (order matches spans). Returns {proposed, minted_hint_ids?, candidates:[{candidate_id, task_id, net, generation, disposition, validation, segment_count, via_count, layers, bend_count, routed_length_mm, length_ratio?, misalignment_mm?}], holds, unresolved_widths, routes_returned, unrouted, stuck, drc_summary, drc_geometric_summary, board_health, stale_candidate_ids, island_deltas?} — unresolved_widths[] names routes NO width could be resolved for (the reply carried no effective_routing_rules.trace_width_mm and no source hint authors a width_mm). Their candidates still land, at width 0.0 with width_source "unresolved", and minerva_pcb_workspace_commit REFUSES them by name (unmodelable_segment, "zero-width copper is not copper") — the copper-creating paths fail closed rather than inventing the 0.25mm literal they used to. Resolve the width (a hint width_mm, or an explicit option) and re-propose — board_health is the worker's whole-board completeness + assembly advisory {complete, missing_copper, partial, assembly:{status, findings}, approximate:true}, enriched panel-side with board_revision and preflight.rendered_this_revision. ROUTE QUALITY: every candidate record carries bend_count and routed_length_mm (zeros for a vias-only candidate), plus length_ratio (routed / per-run manhattan minimum, approximate; absent when that minimum is ~0) and, on single-run candidates, misalignment_mm — the perpendicular offset between the span's endpoints (min(|dx|,|dy|)). THE 2-PIN RULE: on a two-pin span, ANY bend means the pads do not align — length_ratio 1.0 only says the detour is efficient, never that it is necessary; misalignment_mm > 0 says the PLACEMENT is the thing to fix (align with minerva_pcb_move_component snap_to_grid:false, then re-propose) — weigh that before committing. A high ratio or bend count on a longer hop is the same smell at larger scale. HOLDS: a task whose current candidate is PINNED is HELD — the incoming candidate is NOT created and the pin stands, so candidates[] is SHORTER than routes_returned; holds[] names {task_id, held_candidate_id, net, reason} for each. Unpin or reject that candidate (or minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route it) to replace it. Per-component emitter capability notes now ride `emitter_notes` (when non-empty); stuck[] is unrouted pad pairs plus per-hint routing warnings only. TASK CONSTRAINTS ARE CONSUMED: a selected hint whose task carries a routing_constraint (minted by minerva_pcb_add_route_intent's corridor arg, or by a prior minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route corridor/preserve_shape_as_corridor) steers THIS proposal's router run — the stored corridor overrides that hint's own legacy waypoints, if it even has any. Every candidate a constraint steered carries an additive `constraint_revision` key naming which revision produced it. LEGACY MIGRATION: a selected non-'detailed' hint carrying inline waypoints whose task has no routing_constraint yet has that corridor seeded ONCE into a durable task constraint (authored_by "migration") before this run, and the hint's waypoints are then marked superseded and refuse further edits. DRAFT-BOARD COMPOSITION: with a LIVE placement ghost staged, the propose routes against the composed draft — components virtually AT their ghost targets — so the route candidate renders BESIDE the ghost and you see the trace BEFORE the move is accepted. Such candidates carry draft_placements:[{id, component_id, to, status}] (status derived at every read: satisfied=move landed, pending=ghost still live at that pose, invalidated=ghost gone/retargeted) and workspace_commit refuses them until every dependency is satisfied.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_list
tools.description: List the routing workspace: candidates, tasks and selection. Read-only; journals nothing. Args {editor_name, include_terminal?, include_geometry?, task_id?, net?}. Returns {candidates:[…], count, tasks:[{task_id, net, state, span_scoped}], open_task_ids, active_candidate_id, pinned_candidate_ids, stale_candidate_ids}. LIVE candidates only by default — superseded/rejected/committed ones are history and would bury the answers you are deciding between; pass include_terminal:true to see them. Pass include_geometry:true to read each candidate's exact segments/vias — THE pre-commit review object: check the route's actual coordinates against your intent (waypoint adherence, bend placement, corridors) instead of trusting counts and DRC verdicts alone. Candidate records also carry bend_count / routed_length_mm / length_ratio / misalignment_mm — on a 2-pin span ANY bend means the pads do not align (misalignment_mm says by how much); that is a placement fix (freeform move), not a rerouting retry. A candidate's two axes are independent: disposition is the workflow decision, validation is the DRC health (unchecked/checking/clean/violating/stale/error). Candidates routed against a composed draft carry draft_placements:[{id, component_id, to, status: satisfied|pending|invalidated}] — the answer to "can this commit right now" with respect to placement ghosts. VIA GHOSTS SAY WHO THEY ARE FOR: a candidate that is exactly ONE VIA and no copper is a proposed via ENTITY, and its row carries owner_hint_ids + owner — "hint <id>" when minerva_pcb_propose_via was given for_hint (or the human clicked with that hint selected), and "none" plus unowned:true / unowned_note when it was not. An unowned ghost is legal and commits normally; the label exists so "which hint is this via for" is READ off the listing instead of inferred by matching via coordinates to hint segments by eye.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_export_yaml
tools.description: EXPORT the live board as canonical YAML TEXT (SR2FAB S1) — the MCP twin of the Export YAML button, running that button's exact implementation. UNGATED and NON-WRITING: no DRC runs and no file is touched, so a board that minerva_pcb_promote refuses can still be read out, diffed against the file on disk, and archived. Oversized boards ride the by-ref path in both directions (the request snapshots the board; an over-cap document comes back as {yaml_path, yaml_digest} and is read back sha256-verified), so this works on boards far past the 64KiB broker cap. Args {editor_name}. Returns {yaml, bytes, draft:true}. Refuses by name: path_not_supported (a `path` argument is refused rather than ignored — an ignored path returns a success the caller reads as a file having been written), no_board, worker_unavailable, payload_too_large, serialize_failed, serialize_read_failed. THIS IS NOT PROMOTION — the returned document carries no gate verdict, and minerva_pcb_promote remains the only verb that writes the canonical .yaml file. Writing this text over that file yourself bypasses the correctness gate deliberately and silently.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_promote
tools.description: PROMOTE the live board to its canonical YAML file (K13, the serialize-back verb — CORRECTNESS-GATED, COMPLETENESS-ADVISORY per the Epoch UX4 owner ruling): runs the FULL authoritative gate in one call (connectivity DRC + geometric DRC GC1-GC7 + assembly tri-state, composed fail-closed worker-side) and, only when no CORRECTNESS refusal stands, serializes the live board through pcb.serialize and writes it to the adopted document path (or the explicit `path` arg). Any finding, error, or indeterminate refuses by name (promotion_gated, with refusals[] and the three sub-reports) — there is NO acknowledge-through for correctness. A clean-but-PARTIAL board PROMOTES, with the unrouted nets on the reply as advisory.completeness. PANEL-SIDE REGRESSION GUARD: if the prior file has per-net copper (traces ∪ zones ∪ netted vias — a pour counts) or components this promotion would remove, the call refuses copper_regression (regressed_nets, component_delta) unless allow_copper_regression:true. Success reply: {path, digest_sha256, bytes, prior_state, census_delta?, advisory?, staged_drafts?}. Committed candidates and consumed-hint records are NOT mutated — they already describe the copper this file now carries.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_board_check
tools.description: LIVE-BOARD CENSUS (OFC-4, read-only — kills detection-by-refusal): runs the EXACT verdict the promote gate runs — connectivity DRC with per-finding coordinates + the completeness census (complete/missing_copper/partial), geometric DRC GC1-GC7, and the assembly tri-state, composed fail-closed worker-side over the same K2-stripped snapshot of the LIVE board — but writes NOTHING and gates NOTHING: the reply REPORTS the refusals a promote would raise (empty refusals = it would pass). Args {editor_name}. Returns {promotable, refusals, connectivity, geometric, assembly, advisory?}. Before this verb, post-accept damage on the live board was only visible by attempting minerva_pcb_promote and reading its refusal — checkers took yaml|board and the live board had no serialize-out. PARITY (narrowed to the marker channel's honest vocabulary): dangling_endpoint findings refresh the canvas disconnect markers (a clean census clears healed ones); crossing/wrong_net_pad/layer_change_no_via findings ride the reply only. The reply carries board_revision (the revision the verdict describes); if the board changes while the worker runs, the call refuses {error: stale_census, checked_board_revision, current_board_revision} and touches neither markers nor caches — re-run it. A fresh verdict also FEEDS the assembly cache that minerva_pcb_workspace_commit's placement gate consults, so findings you just saw cannot be committed past unacknowledged. Needs the pcb backend; refuses worker_unavailable without it.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_reject
tools.description: REJECT a route candidate: discard it and REOPEN its routing task. Args {editor_name, candidate_id}. Returns the updated candidate record plus stale_candidate_ids. Rejecting is TERMINAL — there is no un-reject, and the way back is a new proposal (minerva_pcb_workspace_propose / _reroute_route), because un-rejecting would resurrect geometry the user already refused. It also marks every still-live candidate's verdict STALE: draft-check is set-scoped, so a verdict computed against a set that included this candidate no longer holds.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_commit
tools.description: COMMIT route candidates (the DCR's Accept): exact geometry becomes REAL COPPER on the board — contiguous same-layer/-width segments chain into ONE polyline trace each (docket 019fce6184c2), plus vias — and each candidate becomes 'committed', in ONE UNDOABLE STEP. Pass EXACTLY ONE of candidate_id (single) or candidate_ids (BATCH, docket 019fd0ab6dd2). A batch is one history entry and ONE undo reverting every member's copper and disposition together, and each member's validation_at_commit is its PRE-batch verdict — sequential single commits would mark clean batch-mates stale purely from the sibling's own revision bump. Single form returns {candidate_id, task_id, task_state, trace_ids, via_ids, consumed_hint_ids, validation_at_commit, candidate, stale_candidate_ids}; batch form returns {results:[per-member], committed_count, trace_ids, via_ids, candidates, stale_candidate_ids}. Source hints are CONSUMED BY RECORD, not deleted. ALL validation precedes ALL mutation across the WHOLE batch: any refusal (illegal transition, unmodelable geometry, duplicate id) leaves the board, dispositions and history untouched and names the offending candidate. Committing an unchecked or violating candidate is allowed and reported, never silently blessed. PLACEMENT ACKNOWLEDGMENT GATE (DCR 019fd5fd9084): when the panel's cached assembly state is FRESH (same board_revision), carries status 'findings', and at least one finding's components intersect the committing candidate's own endpoint components, the commit REFUSES with error 'placement_blocker_unacknowledged' listing blocking_findings — pass acknowledge_placement:true to commit anyway (the reply then records acknowledged_placement_findings). Known findings at the commit point require explicit acknowledgment; a STALE/absent cache or an 'indeterminate' assembly state never blocks — the reply just carries an advisory assembly_note. In a batch, one unacknowledged blocked member refuses the WHOLE batch (all-or-nothing, checked before any copper). tools.name: minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route
tools.description: TRY AGAIN on a whole route: re-run the router scoped to this candidate's own source hints and land a NEW generation for the same task. Args {editor_name, candidate_id, corridor?, preserve_shape_as_corridor?, clear_constraint?, width_mm?, expected_constraint_revision?}. WIDTH (Epoch UX2 station 3): `width_mm` writes the new trace width onto every source hint's kind_payload before the router runs — a durable review-time width change (the reply echoes width_mm; candidates carry width_source:"hint"), landing whether or not the router leg succeeds, and undoable per hint via the hint revision stack. Returns the propose-shaped reply plus {rerouted_candidate_id, prior_task_id, same_task}. The router runs FIRST and the prior candidate is retired only after it answers, so a routing failure never leaves the task with no answer at all. Refused by name when the candidate has already left the live set. HINT-LESS FALLBACK (DCR 01a022ab356c leg C): a candidate whose source hints are GONE (deleted intent) or that never had any (worker attributed []) no longer refuses — the run degrades to task/terminal scoping from the candidate's own endpoints, lands the new generation on the SAME task (superseding, never duplicating) with endpoints carried forward so it stays reroutable, and the reply says so (hintless_fallback: true). Only a candidate with neither hints nor at least two well-formed endpoint pin refs refuses (unscopable_candidate) — an unscopable run must never silently widen to the whole board. Corridor steering is hint-keyed and cannot ride a hint-less run: corridor / preserve_shape_as_corridor on such a candidate refuse steering_unavailable_hintless; clear_constraint remains the recovery path when a constrained task's commit gates stale. STEERING (Epoch UX1 station 9, DCR 019fd095e694, docket 019fd057ea0b comment 1028): `corridor` (Array of {x_mm,y_mm}) REPLACES the candidate's task's durable routing_constraint with this corridor, bumping its revision; `preserve_shape_as_corridor` (bool) DERIVES that new corridor from the candidate's OWN current geometry instead, before this same call reroutes it away — the visible alternative to a hidden 'promote edit to steering' verb. The two are mutually exclusive BY PRESENCE (refused corridor_args_conflict if both keys are sent). CLEARING (Epoch UX2 station 2): `clear_constraint:true` REMOVES the task's routing_constraint — this reroute runs unguided, the owner hint's supersession marker is stripped, and every reply carries cleared_constraint_revision. An intent-shape hint (no waypoints) then stays unguided on every later propose; a hint that DOES carry its own waypoints re-takes authority instead — the next propose re-seeds a corridor from them (station-12 legacy seeding), at a revision above the cleared one (revisions stay monotonic across clears, so stale pre-clear candidates never pass the commit gate). Mutually exclusive (when true) with corridor/preserve_shape_as_corridor; refused no_constraint_to_clear by name on an unconstrained task; expected_constraint_revision guards a clear the same way it guards a steer. `expected_constraint_revision` (int; 0 for an unconstrained task) is optimistic concurrency on the task's constraint — a mismatch refuses constraint_revision_conflict naming the actual revision and steers nothing. preserve_shape_as_corridor is refused multi_span_task when the candidate's task answers more than one hint (no single owner for the derived corridor), and no_single_path when the candidate's own geometry is more than one disconnected run (it is never bridged with a fabricated jump); an explicit corridor:[] is refused corridor_present_but_empty. ALL of these preconditions — candidate exists, its disposition can still reach superseded, its source hints are still present, and (when steering) the task/revision/corridor checks above — are checked BEFORE anything is written. tools.name: minerva_pcb_route_bus_direct
tools.description: Draw a parallel bus of real copper directly — the MCP parity tool for the canvas Bus tool, calling the SAME validation path and the SAME single-journal-step commit. END THE SPINE SHORT OF, OR LEVEL WITH, THE LAST TARGET PAD'S COLUMN — read this before you pick `points`. Each track leaves the bundle at its own departure station and turns to its target, so a spine that RUNS PAST the target column forces every lane to double back, and the crossing/corridor findings that produces read as a placement problem when the spine is the problem. A bus whose spine ends level with the target column usually needs no pin change at all; read the spine before you read the pads. Same rule at the source end: start clear of the source pads. START WITH dry_run: true — it returns the IDENTICAL reply (findings, note, open_nets, clean_order, nets_detail with lane offsets and polylines) with trace_ids/via_ids empty and dry_run: true, and writes NOTHING (board, history and journal untouched), so read the findings first and commit only a bus you have seen; when you want a reviewable on-screen ghost instead of copper, call minerva_pcb_workspace_propose_bus. Takes an ORDERED list of already-declared net names (order is preserved verbatim — never re-sorted, which is what lets a human pick 'the I2S trio' in a specific order and get one net per track in that order) a spine polyline, and one SOURCE and one TARGET pad per net ("Component.Pin" refs, same order as nets, each on its own net); emits one Trace per net running the WHOLE way from its source pad to its target pad — an axis-aligned breakout leg into the bundle, the parallel run, and a leg back out — offset from the spine at clearance-or-better pitch (each net's width auto-derives from its widest EXISTING trace, else the board default, unless width_override is given), mitered through bends so pitch stays constant. Needs 2+ nets and a 2+ point spine after duplicate points are dropped. A BAD BUS STILL COMMITS: when the geometry can be built but breaks a rule (a spine segment shorter than the widest per-net offset so the inner track folds; a pad inside the corridor; two nets' breakout legs that cannot be ordered without crossing; a spine too short for its own fan-outs; two nets closer than their clearance) the traces LAND and the broken rules come back in findings[], each naming the nets and the measured vs required millimetres — copper that exists can be corrected, a refusal leaves nothing to correct. Only a bus with NO geometry is refused: fewer than 2 nets, an undeclared net, a pad ref that does not resolve or sits on another net, a spine of one distinct point, a diagonal spine segment (90-degree bends only), a zero-width track. All N traces land in ONE undoable history step: Ctrl+Z (or PCBData.undo) removes every trace this call created. Returns {trace_ids, via_ids, nets, widths, layer, via_station_layer, findings, open_nets, nets_detail, undo_note, note?} or a named error. RULE: every copper-creating verb returns the coordinates and ids the NEXT verb needs, never ids alone — nets_detail is one entry per net in bus order: {net, lane_index, offset_mm, source, landed, target, traces:[{trace_id, layer, points:[[x_mm,y_mm],...]}] (exactly the board's own polylines), via_id, via?:[x,y], and for an OPEN lane free_end:{trace_id, end:"end"} — the very object minerva_pcb_add_trace takes as its start anchor, pass it verbatim — plus free_end_x_mm/free_end_y_mm/free_end_layer}. OPEN-ENDED BUS: a targets entry of "" lands that net's lane with NO target leg — its trace ends at the end of the lane as a FREE end (no corridor/off-layer finding is raised for a target that does not exist; the open copper is still measured against the board), open_nets lists them and note says how many lanes end open. Finish them later with minerva_pcb_add_trace using start:{trace_id, end} on the open trace, or the canvas Trace tool. Each track peels off the bundle at its own departure station; nothing is ever re-sorted, rerouted or moved to another layer to make a crossing go away — a crossing is reported, not hidden. The spine should be axis-aligned and start clear of the source pads and end clear of the target pads. Example call: {"editor_name": "PCB1", "nets": ["I2S_BCLK", "I2S_LRCLK", "I2S_DATA"], "sources": ["U1.1", "U1.2", "U1.3"], "targets": ["J1.1", "J1.2", "J1.3"], "points": [{"x_mm": 10, "y_mm": 10}, {"x_mm": 30, "y_mm": 10}, {"x_mm": 30, "y_mm": 30}], "layer": "top"}. A BUS MAY CHANGE LAYER ONCE, at a VIA STATION: via_station_index (which vertex of points carries it) plus via_station_layer (the copper the bundle continues on past it), given together — half the pair is refused rather than half-honoured. Every net then gets TWO traces, one per layer run, and ONE through via at that vertex on the station's perpendicular at its own lane offset, all inside the same single undo step; the vias take their pad and drill from the board's design_rules (via_diameter_mm / via_drill_mm, else 0.8 / 0.4). Where the vias need more room across the bundle than the tracks do, the lanes widen locally to the via pitch and come back — that fan-out is the only geometry a station adds. The spine must cross the station STRAIGHT: a station at either END of the spine, or one the spine BENDS at, is refused outright. A station too close to an end for its own fan-out, or a via pitch the lanes cannot widen to without two nets' fan-out legs touching, is a FINDING like every other bad-but-buildable rule — the copper lands and names what broke.

tools.name: minerva_pcb_add_route_intent
tools.description: Author a ROUTE INTENT — connectivity between two pins, no routing performed (Epoch UX1 station 8, DCR 019fd095e694). Atomically creates: (a) a pcb_route_hint annotation carrying ONLY source_pin/dest_pin/note — waypoints is always empty; the corridor NEVER lands on this object. (b) an eagerly-created RouteTask in the routing workspace (task_id "NET|hint_id"): a later propose of THIS hint alone reuses that same task, and a propose that merges this intent's route with another open intent's on the same net (one worker-attributed answer naming both hint ids) ABSORBS both eager tasks into the merged one — carrying over a solitary routing_constraint; two CONFLICTING constraints are KEPT on their surviving singleton tasks (each keeps steering its own hint per-hint, the merged task stays unconstrained, and the conflict is surfaced as constraint_conflicts — Codex 1047 P1-A) — rather than orphaning either eager task or minting a third (cold review H3-1). (c) when `corridor` is given, a routing_constraint stored ON THE TASK ({corridor_points, revision:1, authored_by:"ai", base_board_revision}) — durable steering with one authoritative home, distinct from the connectivity annotation. minerva_pcb_workspace_propose CONSUMES this constraint (Epoch UX1 station 9): it steers that proposal's router run and the landed candidate carries the constraint_revision that produced it. source_pin and dest_pin must already share exactly one net (connect them first with minerva_pcb_connect_net otherwise). Deleting the intent annotation before it is answered cascades: its still-candidate-less eager task is dropped too (a task any candidate has landed on is left alone). Optional `width_mm` (Epoch UX2 station 3) lands on the minted hint's kind_payload — the durable width channel the router already honors (candidates carry width_mm + width_source:"hint") — so trace width is stated WITH the intent instead of patched onto the annotation afterwards; invalid values refuse invalid_width. Returns {success, hint_id, task_id, net, ref?, constraint_revision?, width_mm?, note} where note names the legal next step (minerva_pcb_workspace_propose or minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints with hint_ids:[hint_id]), or a named refusal: pin_unresolvable, cross_net_pins, single_endpoint_only, workspace_unavailable, annotation_rejected. AUTHOR CORRIDORS FROM REAL BOARD CONTEXT (HITL-4): pin coordinates alone do not show footprint bodies, courtyards, or existing copper — read minerva_pcb_get_image / minerva_pcb_spatial_query / minerva_pcb_describe_component (and heed board_health / the load reply's assembly state) BEFORE choosing corridor points, and settle open placement questions before proposing copper through them.

tools.description: Edit ONE candidate's own geometry — the ONE discriminated candidate-edit verb (Epoch UX1 station 10, DCR 019fd095e694, docket 019fd057ea0b comments 1026/1028). EDIT != POLICY: this touches only the named candidate — never its task, never its routing_constraint — and it does NOT pin. To make an edited shape survive the next re-propose, reroute with minerva_pcb_workspace_reroute_route's preserve_shape_as_corridor:true instead; to hold this exact candidate against a batch re-propose, pin it explicitly (minerva_pcb_workspace_pin). Args {editor_name, candidate_id, op, expected_candidate_revision?, …op args}. op == "move_junction" (args point:[x_mm,y_mm], to:[x_mm,y_mm]): junction IDENTITY, not a flattened bend index — a candidate can carry ≥2 DISCONNECTED copper paths (INV-3), and a bend is commonly the shared endpoint of multiple segment ids, so every segment endpoint AND every via coincident with point (within the same tight epsilon the segment graph's own adjacency test uses) moves atomically to to. Refused BY NAME: junction_not_found (nothing coincident with point), ambiguous_junction (point matches junctions on more than one of this candidate's disconnected paths — move each path's junction separately, or supply a point that identifies only one), degenerate_result (the move would collapse a segment to zero length — never emitted, docket 019f9cc3245d). Moving a route's TERMINAL endpoint (the end that anchors a pad on a real board) is an ALLOWED edit, not refused — it detaches the draft's copper from that pad, but this candidate's staled validation and bumped candidate_revision are exactly what a subsequent check/commit exists to report, not a gap this tool needs to close itself. op == "insert_via" (args position:[x_mm,y_mm], from_layer, to_layer): DELEGATES verbatim to the existing RoutingWorkspace.add_via — the path-scoped via/layer edit entry INV-3 names, not reimplemented. Its own named refusals (illegal_via_span, no_segment_at_point, degenerate_insert_at_endpoint, degenerate_insert_on_via, segment_locked, from_layer_mismatch) pass through unchanged. CONCURRENCY (symmetric with station 9's expected_constraint_revision): expected_candidate_revision, when given, is checked against the candidate's CURRENT candidate_revision BEFORE either op runs — a mismatch refuses candidate_revision_conflict {candidate_id, expected_candidate_revision, actual_candidate_revision} and mutates nothing; a successful edit bumps candidate_revision and the reply reports the new one — chain a second edit with THAT number, not whatever was read before this call. Both ops refuse a TERMINAL candidate (committed/rejected/superseded) by name (candidate_not_editable) — a terminal candidate is a record, not a draft.

skills.title: PCB design (IR-compiled, fail-closed DRC/routing/CAM)
skills.summary: Sole PCB surface (the in-tree editor and .minpcb are retired; boards are .pcbskel documents). Author canonical YAML (docs/board-yaml.md) or place parts with minerva_pcb_add_component/minerva_pcb_connect_net, then load with minerva_pcb_load_board. minerva_pcb_validate checks structure; minerva_pcb_drc checks net connectivity; minerva_pcb_drc_geometric compiles to the ResolvedBoard IR and checks real copper (width, clearance, drill, annular ring, edge, hole spacing) — fail-closed, so 'indeterminate' is not a pass. Routing is IR-native and fail-closed too: author pcb_route_hint annotations, run minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints (or minerva_pcb_workspace_propose) to land RouteCandidates in the routing workspace, then resolve each with minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/minerva_pcb_workspace_reject. minerva_pcb_generate emits KiCad text; minerva_pcb_gerbers emits Gerber+Excellon output — both resolve footprints from a locked seed library and fail closed rather than approximate copper. minerva_pcb_check_libraries/minerva_pcb_check_bom check parts against a separate KiCAD subset minerva_pcb_fetch_libraries downloads. Parts go on BY LIBRARY REF: minerva_pcb_add_component {footprint: "LibNick:PartName"} lands the library's own pads, silk and courtyard and is fabricable at once, while the generic types (HEADER, RESISTOR, IC_QFP, ...) are sketch geometry no fab can build; every reply says which you got in geometry.fabricable. minerva_pcb_footprint_report shows a ref's pad facts and a picture before you place it. Review commentary is written with Minerva's CORE annotation kinds through minerva_annotations_add - 2d_arrow to point AT something, 2d_text to label, 2d_region for an area, 2d_polyline for a path - in board millimetres.
skills.preconditions: A PCB editor tab is open (minerva_list_editors) or spawned via minerva_create_plugin_editor (editor_item_id "new_pcb"); the board-YAML tools (validate/generate/gerbers/drc/drc_geometric/check_libraries/check_bom) take board text directly and need no open editor.
skills.outcome: The board renders with real components, nets and routed copper; minerva_pcb_validate and both DRC tools report clean or name exactly what is wrong and where; minerva_pcb_gerbers/minerva_pcb_generate produce fabrication files traceable to the same footprint geometry DRC checked; route proposals are inspectable before they become copper. Annotations land on what they name: minerva_annotations_list resolves each one's anchor_detail to the intended pad/via/component/trace, and the rendered board image agrees.
skills.steps:
1. Open the editor tab (minerva_list_editors) or create one (minerva_create_plugin_editor, editor_item_id "new_pcb").
2. Author canonical YAML or place parts with minerva_pcb_add_component/minerva_pcb_connect_net, then minerva_pcb_load_board. Place BY LIBRARY REF (footprint "LibNick:PartName") - check the ref first with minerva_pcb_footprint_report, or minerva_pcb_acquire_footprint when the library lacks it - and read geometry.fabricable in the reply. A generic sketch type is placement-only: it makes the whole board's geometric DRC and every pour fill indeterminate until it resolves or goes.
3. Validate with minerva_pcb_validate; check minerva_pcb_library_status once (minerva_pcb_fetch_libraries if needed), then minerva_pcb_check_libraries/minerva_pcb_check_bom.
4. Route: add pcb_route_hint annotations (minerva_annotations_add), minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints (commit=false) or minerva_pcb_workspace_propose to land candidates, then minerva_pcb_workspace_commit/minerva_pcb_workspace_reject each candidate_id — or re-run apply_route_hints with commit=true.
5. Run minerva_pcb_drc and minerva_pcb_drc_geometric on the finished board; 'indeterminate' blocks, it is not a pass.
6. Export with minerva_pcb_generate and minerva_pcb_gerbers; a human must still eyeball the output before real fabrication.
7. Annotate (at any point, for review commentary - not for routing): read the target's exact board mm from minerva_pcb_pin_info, then minerva_annotations_add {editor_name, annotation: {"kind": "2d_arrow", "schema_version": 2, "anchor": {"plugin": "core", "type": "canvas.point", "id": {"x": 22.0, "y": 92.95}, "snapshot": {"position": [22.0, 92.95]}}, "kind_payload": {"label": "here"}, "primitives": [{"kind": "arrow", "from": [28.0, 87.0], "to": [22.0, 92.95]}], "lifecycle": "open", "author": {"kind": "ai"}, "view_context": "pcb", "visible_in_views": ["all"], "summary": "here"}} - `to` is the pad, `from` is clear space 5-8 mm behind it.
8. Verify every annotation you add: minerva_annotations_list must report anchor_detail naming the entity you meant, with distance_mm near 0 and primitives.to within 0.5 mm of anchor_detail.position; then minerva_pcb_get_image (save_to_path, and read the PNG back) to see the head land on the part. Dragging an annotation with the transform tool rewrites its primitives but never its anchor block, so anchor.id/snapshot drift from where it now points - re-add rather than drag when the anchor matters.
skills.system_prompt: Sole PCB surface; the legacy in-tree editor is gone. Routing, DRC and CAM share one ResolvedBoard IR compiler and one rule: canvas may degrade, but routing/DRC/CAM never approximate copper — unresolvable geometry fails closed. minerva_pcb_drc is connectivity-only; minerva_pcb_drc_geometric is the real copper check and must pass before fabrication. minerva_pcb_apply_route_hints always proposes before it commits. minerva_pcb_resolve exposes resolved silk/courtyard geometry directly (compile already does this internally for gerbers/generate/drc_geometric); minerva_pcb_normalize migrates legacy inline pin geometry to the current schema. Board coordinates are millimetres, y-down, one frame shared by every pcb verb AND by annotations - never screen pixels. Commentary uses the core kinds: 2d_arrow points AT a thing (its `to` IS the target, `from` is empty space behind it), 2d_text labels a spot, 2d_region calls out an area, 2d_polyline traces a path. pcb_route_hint is workflow-class - it steers the router (step 4) and is never the way to point something out. The core 2d_* kinds accept ONLY a core/canvas.point anchor: a pcb/pad or pcb/component anchor on one is refused as kind_anchor_incompatible and the add returns no id. The board entity is resolved GEOMETRICALLY instead - minerva_annotations_list hit-tests the kind's own anchor point (an arrow's tip, a text's `at`) against the live board, so putting the tip on the pad is exactly what makes anchor_detail read {kind: "pad", id: "R8A.1"}. Anchor to a pad, component, net or trace only for pcb_route_hint, which accepts pcb/pad. minerva_pcb_describe_region returns the annotations inside a rectangle as its `notes`.
